title.en: Volume 66 Biographies 16: Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui

sentences.zh: 王珪王珪，字叔玠，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Gui, styled Shujie, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, styled Shujie, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 在魏爲烏丸氏，曾祖神念，自魏奔梁，復姓王氏。

translations.literal: Under Wei they were the Wuhuan clan. His great-grandfather Shennian fled from Wei to Liang and restored the surname Wang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wei dynasty the family bore the Wuhuan clan name. His great-grandfather Shennian fled from Wei to Liang and took the surname Wang once again.

sentences.zh: 祖僧辯，梁太尉、尚書令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengbian was Grand Marshal and Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengbian had served Liang as Grand Marshal and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父顗，北齊樂陵太守。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Administrator of Leling in Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi had been Administrator of Leling under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 珪幼孤，性雅澹，少嗜欲，志量沉深，能安於貧賤，體道履正，交不苟合。

translations.literal: Gui lost his father while young. His nature was refined and calm; he had few desires. His ambition and capacity were deep and profound. He could content himself in poverty and low station, embodied the Way and walked in righteousness, and would not associate with others lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Gui lost his father while still young. Refined and calm by nature, with few desires, he possessed deep ambition and a steady mind. He could live contentedly in poverty, embodied the Way in his conduct, and would not enter friendships lightly.

sentences.zh: 季叔頗，當時通儒，有人倫之鑑，嘗謂所親曰：「門戸所寄，唯在此兒耳。」

translations.literal: His younger uncle Po was a renowned scholar of the time with a keen eye for human character. He once told those close to him: "The hope of our house rests entirely on this boy alone.
translations.idiomatic: His younger uncle Po was a leading scholar of the day with a sharp eye for character. He once told those close to him, "The future of our house rests on this boy alone.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，爲奉禮郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaihuang era, he served as Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaihuang era he was appointed Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 及頗坐漢王諒反事被誅，珪當從坐，遂亡命於南山，積十餘歲。

translations.literal: When Po was executed for involvement in Prince of Han Liang's rebellion, Gui was liable to share punishment as an associate. He fled into the South Mountains and lived as a fugitive for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Po was executed for his part in the Prince of Han's rebellion, Gui faced punishment as an associate and fled into the South Mountains, where he remained a fugitive for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，丞相府司錄李綱薦珪貞諒有器識，引爲世子府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu entered the pass, Li Gang, Registrar of the Chancellor's Office, recommended Gui for his integrity and capacity for discernment, and he was appointed Advisory Assessor in the Heir Apparent's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu entered the pass, Li Gang, Registrar of the Chancellor's Office, recommended Gui as a man of integrity and discernment, and he was appointed Advisory Assessor in the Heir Apparent's Office.

sentences.zh: 及東宮建，除太子中舍人；

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Aide to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Aide to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋轉中允，甚爲太子所禮。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to Principal Mentor and was greatly honored by the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Principal Mentor and was greatly honored by the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 後以連其陰謀事，流於巂州。

translations.literal: Later, for connection with the crown prince's secret plotting, he was exiled to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his connection with the crown prince's secret plotting, he was exiled to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 建成誅後，太宗素知其才，召拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: After Jian Cheng was executed, Emperor Taizong, who had long known his talent, summoned him and appointed him Remonstrating Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Jiancheng was executed, Emperor Taizong, who had long known his ability, summoned him and appointed him Remonstrating Adviser.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，太宗嘗謂侍臣曰：「正主御邪臣，不能致理；

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, Taizong once told his attending officials: "An upright ruler with wicked ministers cannot achieve good governance;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan, Taizong once told his attending officials, "An upright ruler with wicked ministers cannot bring about good order;

sentences.zh: 正臣事邪主，亦不能致理，唯君臣相遇，有同魚水，則海內可安也。

translations.literal: upright ministers serving a wicked ruler also cannot achieve good governance. Only when ruler and minister meet like fish and water can the realm be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: nor can upright ministers serving a wicked ruler bring about good order. Only when ruler and minister meet like fish and water can the realm be at peace.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖，田舍翁耳。

translations.literal: In old times, Emperor Gaozu of Han was nothing but a farmer.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Emperor Gaozu of Han was nothing but a farmer.

sentences.zh: 提三尺劍定天下，既而規模弘遠，慶流子孫者，此蓋任得賢臣所致也。

translations.literal: He took up a three-foot sword and settled the realm; thereafter his broad vision and blessings that flowed to his descendants were surely brought about by employing worthy ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He took up a three-foot sword and settled the realm, and the broad vision and blessings that passed to his descendants were surely brought about by employing worthy ministers.

sentences.zh: 朕雖不明，幸諸公數相匡救，冀憑嘉謀，致天下於太平耳。」

translations.literal: I, though not enlightened, am fortunate that you all often set me right. I hope through your excellent counsel to bring the realm to peace.
translations.idiomatic: I am not enlightened, but I am fortunate that you all often set me right. I hope through your excellent counsel to bring the realm to peace.

sentences.zh: 珪對曰：「臣聞木從繩則正，後從諫則聖。

translations.literal: Gui replied: "I have heard that wood follows the line and becomes straight, and a ruler who heeds remonstrance becomes sage.
translations.idiomatic: Gui replied, "I have heard that wood follows the line and becomes straight, and a ruler who heeds remonstrance becomes sage.

sentences.zh: 故古者聖主，必有諍臣七人，言而不用，則相繼以死。

translations.literal: Therefore in antiquity sage rulers necessarily had seven remonstrating ministers who, if their words went unheeded, would one after another die in their effort.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in antiquity sage rulers always had seven remonstrating ministers who, if their words went unheeded, would one after another die in the effort.

sentences.zh: 陛下開聖慮，納芻蕘，臣處不諱之朝，實願罄其狂瞽。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty opens your sage understanding and accepts humble counsel. I serve in a court where nothing is taboo, and I truly wish to pour forth all my ignorant and misguided words."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty opens your sage understanding and accepts humble counsel. I serve in a court where nothing is taboo, and I truly wish to pour forth all my ignorant and misguided words."

sentences.zh: 太宗稱善，敕自今後中書門下及三品以上入閣，必遣諫官隨之。

translations.literal: Taizong praised this and ordered that from then on, whenever officials of the Central Secretariat and Chancellery and those of third rank or higher entered the inner hall, remonstrating officials must accompany them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong praised this and ordered that from then on, whenever officials of the Central Secretariat and Chancellery and those of third rank or higher entered the inner hall, remonstrating officials must accompany them.

sentences.zh: 珪每推誠納忠，多所獻替，太宗顧待益厚，賜爵永寧縣男，遷黃門侍郎，兼太子右庶子。

translations.literal: Gui ever offered loyal sincerity and made many proposals for improvement. Taizong's regard for him grew ever deeper. He was granted the title Baron of Yongning County, promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and concurrently appointed Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Gui ever offered loyal sincerity and made many proposals for improvement. Taizong's regard for him grew ever deeper. He was granted the title Baron of Yongning County, promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and concurrently appointed Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年，代高士廉爲侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year, he replaced Gao Shilian as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he replaced Gao Shilian as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗閒居，與珪宴語，時有美人侍側，本廬江王瑗之姬，瑗敗籍沒入宮，太宗指示之曰：「廬江不道，賊殺其夫而納其室。

translations.literal: Taizong once while at leisure conversed with Gui at a feast. A beautiful woman waited at his side — originally a concubine of Prince of Lujiang Yuan. When Yuan was defeated, she was seized and entered the palace. Taizong pointed to her and said: "The Prince of Lujiang was wicked. Like a bandit he killed her husband and took her into his household.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while at leisure, Taizong conversed with Gui over a feast. A beautiful woman waited at his side — originally a concubine of the Prince of Lujiang. When the prince was defeated she was seized and entered the palace. Taizong pointed to her and said, "The Prince of Lujiang was wicked. Like a bandit he killed her husband and took her for himself.

sentences.zh: 暴虐之甚，何有不亡者乎！」

translations.literal: His cruelty was extreme — how could he not perish!
translations.idiomatic: His cruelty was so extreme — how could he not perish!

sentences.zh: 珪避席曰：「陛下以廬江取此婦人爲是耶，爲非耶？」

translations.literal: Gui rose from his seat and said: "Does Your Majesty consider it right or wrong that the Prince of Lujiang took this woman?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui rose from his seat and said, "Does Your Majesty consider it right or wrong that the Prince of Lujiang took this woman?"

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「殺人而取其妻，卿乃問朕是非，何也？」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "He killed a man and took his wife — and you ask me whether it was right or wrong. Why?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "He killed a man and took his wife — and you ask me whether it was right or wrong. Why?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣聞於管子曰：『齊桓公之郭，問其父老曰：『郭何故亡？』

translations.literal: He replied: "I have heard in Guanzi that when Duke Huan of Qi passed through Guo, he asked the elders: 'Why did Guo perish?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have read in Guanzi that when Duke Huan of Qi passed through Guo, he asked the elders, 'Why did Guo perish?

sentences.zh: 父老曰：『以其善善而惡惡也。』

translations.literal: The elders said: 'Because he favored what should be favored and hated what should be hated.
translations.idiomatic: The elders said, 'Because he favored what should be favored and hated what should be hated.

sentences.zh: 桓公曰：『若子之言，乃賢君也，何至於亡？』

translations.literal: The duke said: 'If what you say is true, that was an worthy ruler — how could he have perished?
translations.idiomatic: The duke said, 'If what you say is true, that was a worthy ruler — how could he have perished?

sentences.zh: 父老曰：『不然，郭君善善而不能用，惡惡而不能去，所以亡也。』

translations.literal: The elders said: 'It is not so. The lord of Guo favored what should be favored but could not employ the good; he hated what should be hated but could not remove the wicked. That is why Guo perished.
translations.idiomatic: The elders said, 'It is not so. The lord of Guo favored what should be favored but could not employ the good; he hated what should be hated but could not remove the wicked. That is why Guo perished.

sentences.zh: 今此婦人尚在左右，竊以聖心爲是之，陛下若以爲非，此謂知惡而不去也。」

translations.literal: Today this woman is still at your side. I privately take it that Your Majesty's sacred heart approves of this. If Your Majesty considers it wrong, this is knowing what is wicked yet not removing it."
translations.idiomatic: Today this woman is still at your side. I privately take it that Your Majesty's sacred heart approves of this. If Your Majesty considers it wrong, this is knowing what is wicked yet not removing it."

sentences.zh: 太宗雖不出此美人，而甚重其言。

translations.literal: Although Taizong did not dismiss this woman, he greatly valued Gui's words.
translations.idiomatic: Although Taizong did not dismiss this woman, he greatly valued Gui's words.

sentences.zh: 時太常少卿祖孝孫以教宮人聲樂不稱旨，爲太宗所讓。

translations.literal: At that time Zu Xiaosun, Vice Minister of Ceremonies, was reproached by Taizong because the palace women's music he taught did not meet his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zu Xiaosun, Vice Minister of Ceremonies, was reproached by Taizong because the palace women's music he taught did not please him.

sentences.zh: 珪及溫彥博諫曰：「孝孫妙解音律，非不用心，但恐陛下顧問不得其人，以惑陛下視聽。

translations.literal: Gui and Wen Yanbo remonstrated: "Xiaosun has a masterly understanding of music; it is not that he is negligent. I only fear that those Your Majesty consults are not the right people, and so mislead Your Majesty's sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and Wen Yanbo remonstrated, "Xiaosun has a masterly understanding of music; it is not that he is negligent. I only fear that those Your Majesty consults are not the right people and so mislead Your Majesty's sight and hearing.

sentences.zh: 且孝孫雅士，陛下忽爲教女樂而怪之，臣恐天下怪愕。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Xiaosun is a refined gentleman. Your Majesty suddenly blames him for teaching female musicians — I fear the realm will be astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Xiaosun is a refined gentleman. Your Majesty suddenly blames him for teaching female musicians — I fear the realm will be astonished.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒曰：「卿皆我之腹心，當進忠獻直，何乃附下罔上，反爲孝孫言也！」

translations.literal: Taizong angrily said: "You are all my closest advisers. You should offer loyal and forthright counsel — why do you instead fawn on subordinates and deceive your superior, speaking on Xiaosun's behalf!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong angrily said, "You are all my closest advisers. You should offer loyal and forthright counsel — why do you instead fawn on subordinates and deceive your superior, speaking on Xiaosun's behalf!"

sentences.zh: 彥博拜謝，珪獨不拜。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo bowed in apology; Gui alone did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo bowed in apology; Gui alone did not bow.

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣本事前宮，罪已當死。

translations.literal: He said: "I once served the former palace — my crime already deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I once served the former palace — my crime already deserved death.

sentences.zh: 陛下矜恕性命，不以不肖，置之樞近，責以忠直。

translations.literal: Your Majesty spared my life out of compassion and, despite my unworthiness, placed me near the inner councils, demanding loyalty and forthrightness from me.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty spared my life out of compassion and, despite my unworthiness, placed me near the inner councils, demanding loyalty and forthrightness from me.

sentences.zh: 今臣所言，豈是爲私？

translations.literal: What I say now — is it for private ends?
translations.idiomatic: What I say now — is it for private ends?

sentences.zh: 不意陛下忽以疑事誚臣，是陛下負臣，臣不負陛下。」

translations.literal: I did not expect Your Majesty suddenly to rebuke me on a matter of doubt. It is Your Majesty who has wronged me; I have not wronged Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect Your Majesty suddenly to rebuke me on a matter of doubt. It is Your Majesty who has wronged me; I have not wronged Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 帝默然而罷。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent and let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 翌日，帝謂房玄齡曰：「自古帝王，能納諫者固難矣。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor said to Fang Xuanling: "Since antiquity, it has been difficult for emperors to accept remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor said to Fang Xuanling, "Since antiquity, it has been difficult for emperors to accept remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 昔周武王尚不用伯夷、叔齊，宣王賢主，杜伯猶以無罪見殺，吾夙夜庶幾前聖，恨不能仰及古人。

translations.literal: In old times even King Wu of Zhou did not employ Bo Yi and Shu Qi. King Xuan was an worthy ruler, yet Duke Du was still killed though innocent. Day and night I aspire to the sages of old, yet regret that I cannot reach up to the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: In former times even King Wu of Zhou did not employ Bo Yi and Shu Qi. King Xuan was a worthy ruler, yet Duke Du was still killed though innocent. Day and night I aspire to the sages of old, yet regret that I cannot reach up to the ancients.

sentences.zh: 昨責彥博、王珪，朕甚悔之。

translations.literal: Yesterday when I rebuked Yanbo and Wang Gui, I deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday when I rebuked Yanbo and Wang Gui, I deeply regretted it.

sentences.zh: 公等勿以此而不進直言也。」

translations.literal: Do not let this keep you from offering forthright counsel."
translations.idiomatic: Do not let this keep you from offering forthright counsel."

sentences.zh: 時房玄齡、李靖、溫彥博、戴胄、魏徵與珪同知國政。

translations.literal: At that time Fang Xuanling, Li Jing, Wen Yanbo, Dai Zhou, Wei Zheng, and Gui jointly oversaw state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fang Xuanling, Li Jing, Wen Yanbo, Dai Zhou, Wei Zheng, and Gui jointly oversaw state affairs.

sentences.zh: 後嘗侍宴，太宗謂珪曰：「卿識鑑清通，尤善談論，自房玄齡等，咸宜品藻，又可自量，孰與諸子賢？」

translations.literal: Later, while attending a feast, Taizong said to Gui: "Your discernment is clear and penetrating, and you are especially skilled in discussion. You should appraise Fang Xuanling and the others, and also assess yourself — which of you is most worthy?
translations.idiomatic: Later, while attending a feast, Taizong said to Gui, "Your discernment is clear and penetrating, and you are especially skilled in discussion. You should appraise Fang Xuanling and the others, and also assess yourself — which of you is most worthy?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「孜孜奉國，知無不爲，臣不如玄齡；

translations.literal: He replied: "In diligent service to the state, knowing nothing he ought not to do — I am not the equal of Xuanling;
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In diligent service to the state, knowing nothing he ought not to do — I am not the equal of Xuanling;

sentences.zh: 才兼文武，出將入相，臣不如李靖；

translations.literal: in talent combining civil and military, going forth as general and entering as chancellor — I am not the equal of Li Jing;
translations.idiomatic: in talent combining civil and military, going forth as general and entering as chancellor — I am not the equal of Li Jing;

sentences.zh: 敷奏詳明，出納惟允，臣不如溫彥博；

translations.literal: in detailed and lucid memorials, in receiving and issuing with perfect fairness — I am not the equal of Wen Yanbo;
translations.idiomatic: in detailed and lucid memorials, in receiving and issuing with perfect fairness — I am not the equal of Wen Yanbo;

sentences.zh: 處繁理劇，眾務必舉，臣不如戴胄；

translations.literal: in handling complexity and resolving urgency, ensuring every task is accomplished — I am not the equal of Dai Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: in handling complexity and resolving urgency, ensuring every task is accomplished — I am not the equal of Dai Zhou;

sentences.zh: 以諫諍爲心，恥君不及於堯、舜，臣不如魏徵。

translations.literal: in taking remonstrance as his heart's purpose, ashamed that his ruler falls short of Yao and Shun — I am not the equal of Wei Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: in taking remonstrance as his heart's purpose, ashamed that his ruler falls short of Yao and Shun — I am not the equal of Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 至如激濁揚清，嫉惡好善，臣於數子，亦有一日之長。」

translations.literal: As for stirring the muddy and lifting the clear, hating wickedness and loving goodness — among these several men I too have my own day-long strength.
translations.idiomatic: As for stirring the muddy and lifting the clear, hating wickedness and loving goodness — among these several men I too have my own day-long strength.

sentences.zh: 太宗深然其言，群公亦各以爲盡己所懷，謂之確論。

translations.literal: Taizong deeply approved his words. The assembled ministers each felt he had fully expressed what was in their hearts, and called it a definitive assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong deeply approved his words. The assembled ministers each felt he had fully expressed what was in their hearts, and called it a definitive assessment.

sentences.zh: 後進爵爲郡公。

translations.literal: Later he was advanced to the rank of Grand Duke of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was advanced to the rank of Grand Duke of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 七年，坐漏洩禁中語，左遷同州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, for leaking forbidden words from within the palace, he was demoted to Prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, for leaking forbidden words from within the palace, he was demoted to Prefect of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，召拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: The following year he was recalled and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled and appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十一年，與諸儒正定《五禮》，書成，賜帛三百段，封一子爲縣男。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, together with various Confucian scholars he corrected and fixed the 《Five Rites》. When the work was complete, he was granted three hundred bolts of silk and one son was enfeoffed as Baron of a County.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, together with various Confucian scholars he corrected and fixed the 《Five Rites》. When the work was complete, he was granted three hundred bolts of silk and one son was enfeoffed as Baron of a County.

sentences.zh: 是歲，兼魏王師。

translations.literal: That same year he was additionally appointed tutor to the Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was additionally appointed tutor to the Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 既而上問黃門侍郎韋挺曰：「王珪爲魏王泰師，與其相見，若爲禮節？」

translations.literal: After this the emperor questioned Vice Director Wei Ting: "Wang Gui is tutor to Li Tai, Prince of Wei. What should the etiquette be when they meet?
translations.idiomatic: After this the emperor questioned Vice Director Wei Ting, "Wang Gui is tutor to Li Tai, Prince of Wei. What should the etiquette be when they meet?

sentences.zh: 挺對曰：「見師之禮，拜答如禮。」

translations.literal: Wei Ting replied: "The etiquette of meeting one's teacher — bow and respond according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ting replied, "The etiquette of meeting one's teacher — bow and respond according to ritual."

sentences.zh: 王問珪以忠孝，珪答曰：「陛下，王之君也，事君思盡忠；

translations.literal: The prince asked Gui about loyalty and filial piety. Gui answered: "Your Majesty is the prince's ruler — in serving a ruler one should think of utmost loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked Gui about loyalty and filial piety. Gui answered, "Your Majesty is the prince's ruler — in serving a ruler one should think of utmost loyalty;

sentences.zh: 陛下，王之父也，事父思盡孝。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is the prince's father — in serving a father one should think of utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is the prince's father — in serving a father one should think of utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 忠孝之道，可以立身，可以成名，當年可以享天祐，余芳可以垂後葉。」

translations.literal: The Way of loyalty and filial piety can establish one's person and make one's name. In one's own lifetime one may enjoy Heaven's blessing; its lingering fragrance can pass down to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of loyalty and filial piety can establish one's person and make one's name. In one's own lifetime one may enjoy Heaven's blessing; its lingering fragrance can pass down to later generations.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「忠孝之道，已聞教矣，願聞所習。」

translations.literal: The prince said: "I have heard your teaching on the Way of loyalty and filial piety. I wish to hear what one should study."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "I have heard your teaching on the Way of loyalty and filial piety. I wish to hear what one should study."

sentences.zh: 珪答曰：「漢東平王蒼云：『爲善最樂。』」

translations.literal: Gui replied: "Liu Cang, Prince of Dongping of Han, said: 'Doing good is the greatest joy.'
translations.idiomatic: Gui replied, "Liu Cang, Prince of Dongping of Han, said, 'Doing good is the greatest joy.'

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「古來帝子，生於宮闥，及其成人，無不驕逸，是以傾覆相踵，少能自濟。

translations.literal: The emperor told his attending officials: "Imperial sons since antiquity, born within the palace gates, when they come of age have none who were not arrogant and dissolute. Therefore ruin has followed one after another, and few have been able to save themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attending officials, "Imperial sons since antiquity, born within the palace gates, when they come of age have none who were not arrogant and dissolute. Therefore ruin has followed one after another, and few have been able to save themselves.

sentences.zh: 我今嚴教子弟，欲令皆得安全。

translations.literal: I now strictly instruct my sons and younger brothers, wishing that all may reach safety.
translations.idiomatic: I now strictly instruct my sons and younger brothers, wishing that all may reach safety.

sentences.zh: 王珪我久驅使，是所諳悉，以其意存忠孝，選爲子師。

translations.literal: I have long employed Wang Gui and know him well. Because his intentions rest in loyalty and filial piety, I have chosen him as my son's tutor.
translations.idiomatic: I have long employed Wang Gui and know him well. Because his intentions rest in loyalty and filial piety, I have chosen him as my son's tutor.

sentences.zh: 爾宜語泰：『汝之待珪，如事我也，可以無過。』」

translations.literal: You should tell Tai: 'In the way you treat Gui, treat him as you would treat me — then you may be without fault."
translations.idiomatic: You should tell Tai, 'In the way you treat Gui, treat him as you would treat me — then you may be without fault."

sentences.zh: 泰每爲之先拜，珪亦以師道自居，物議善之。

translations.literal: Tai would each time bow to Gui first, and Gui also held himself to the role of teacher. Public opinion approved."
translations.idiomatic: Tai would each time bow to Gui first, and Gui also held himself to the role of teacher. Public opinion approved."

sentences.zh: 時珪子敬直尚南平公主。

translations.literal: At that time Gui's son Jingzhi was married to Princess Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gui's son Jingzhi was married to Princess Nanping.

sentences.zh: 禮有婦見舅姑之儀，自近代公主出降，此禮皆廢。

translations.literal: Ritual provides for the ceremony of a wife presenting herself to her husband's parents. Since recent times, when princesses were given in marriage, this ceremony had all been abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual provides for the ceremony of a wife presenting herself to her husband's parents. Since recent times, when princesses were given in marriage, this ceremony had all been abandoned.

sentences.zh: 珪曰：「今主上欽明，動循法制。

translations.literal: Gui said: "Now our sovereign is reverent and enlightened, and in every action follows the laws and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "Now our sovereign is reverent and enlightened, and in every action follows the laws and institutions.

sentences.zh: 吾受公主謁見，豈爲身榮，所以成國家之美耳。」

translations.literal: That I accept the princess's visit — is it for my personal glory? It is to complete the beauty of the state's institutions.
translations.idiomatic: That I accept the princess's visit — is it for my personal glory? It is to complete the beauty of the state's institutions.

sentences.zh: 遂與其妻就席而坐，令公主親執笄行盥饋之道，禮成而退。

translations.literal: Thereupon he and his wife took their seats, and had the princess personally hold the hairpin and perform the hand-washing and food-serving rites. When the ceremony was complete she withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he and his wife took their seats, and had the princess personally hold the hairpin and perform the hand-washing and food-serving rites. When the ceremony was complete she withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是後公主下降有舅姑者，皆備婦禮，自珪始也。

translations.literal: Thereafter whenever a princess married where she had parents-in-law, the full rites of a wife were observed — beginning with Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter whenever a princess married where she had parents-in-law, the full rites of a wife were observed — beginning with Gui.

sentences.zh: 珪少時貧寒，人或遺之，初不辭謝；

translations.literal: In his youth Gui was poor and cold; when people gave him gifts, at first he did not refuse or thank them;
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Gui was poor and cold; when people gave him gifts, at first he did not refuse or thank them;

sentences.zh: 及貴，皆厚報之，雖其人已亡，必賑贍其妻子。

translations.literal: when he became eminent, he generously repaid them all. Even if the giver had already died, he would certainly provide relief for his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: when he became eminent, he generously repaid them all. Even if the giver had already died, he would certainly provide relief for his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 事寡嫂盡禮，撫孤侄恩義極隆，宗姻困匱者，亦多所周恤。

translations.literal: He treated his widowed sister-in-law with full propriety. In raising his orphaned nephews his benevolence and righteousness were utmost. Kinsmen in hardship he also often supported.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his widowed sister-in-law with full propriety. In raising his orphaned nephews his benevolence and righteousness were utmost. Kinsmen in hardship he also often supported.

sentences.zh: 珪通貴漸久，而不營私廟，四時蒸嘗，猶祭於寢。

translations.literal: Gui had long been prominent, yet he did not establish a private ancestral temple. For the seasonal offerings he still sacrificed in his bedroom.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had long been prominent, yet he did not establish a private ancestral temple. For the seasonal offerings he still sacrificed in his bedroom.

sentences.zh: 坐爲法司所劾，太宗優容，弗之譴也，因爲立廟，以愧其心。

translations.literal: For this he was impeached by the judicial authorities. Taizong showed him forbearance and did not punish him, but had a temple built for him to shame his conscience.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was impeached by the judicial authorities. Taizong showed him forbearance and did not punish him, but had a temple built for him to shame his conscience.

sentences.zh: 珪既儉不中禮，時論以是少之。

translations.literal: Gui was frugal to the point of failing ritual propriety, and contemporary opinion on this account slighted him somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was frugal to the point of failing ritual propriety, and contemporary opinion on this account slighted him somewhat.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遇疾，敕公主就第省視，又遣民部尚書唐儉增損藥膳。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he fell ill. An edict ordered the princess to his residence to visit him, and Minister of Revenue Tang Jian was dispatched to adjust his medicines and diet.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he fell ill. An edict ordered the princess to his residence to visit him, and Minister of Revenue Tang Jian was dispatched to adjust his medicines and diet.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: Soon after he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he died, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 太宗素服舉哀於別次，悼惜久之。

translations.literal: Taizong wore plain garments and mourned in a separate hall, grieving for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wore plain garments and mourned in a separate hall, grieving for a long time.

sentences.zh: 詔魏王泰率百官親往臨哭，贈吏部尚書，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Li Tai, Prince of Wei, to lead all officials in person to attend the mourning. He was posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Li Tai, Prince of Wei, to lead all officials in person to attend the mourning. He was posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 長子崇基，襲爵，官至主爵郎中。

translations.literal: His eldest son Chongji inherited the title and rose to the office of Director in the Ministry of Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Chongji inherited the title and rose to the office of Director in the Ministry of Enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 少子敬直，以尚主拜附馬都尉，坐與太子承乾交結，徙於嶺外。

translations.literal: His youngest son Jingzhi, through marriage to the princess, was appointed Commandant of Escorts. For association with Crown Prince Chenggan he was exiled beyond the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Jingzhi, through marriage to the princess, was appointed Commandant of Escorts. For association with Crown Prince Chenggan he was exiled beyond the mountains.

sentences.zh: 崇基孫旭，開元初，爲左司郎中，兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Chongji's grandson Xu, in the early Kaiyuan era, served as Director of the Left Department and concurrently as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji's grandson Xu, in the early Kaiyuan era, served as Director of the Left Department and concurrently as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 時光祿少卿盧崇道犯罪配流嶺南，逃歸匿於東都，爲讎家所發。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Chongdao, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, having been convicted and sentenced to exile in Lingnan, escaped and hid in the Eastern Capital, where he was denounced by an enemy family.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lu Chongdao, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, having been convicted and sentenced to exile in Lingnan, escaped and hid in the Eastern Capital, where he was denounced by an enemy family.

sentences.zh: 玄宗令旭究其獄，旭欲擅其威權，因捕系崇道親黨數十人，皆極其楚毒，然後結成其罪，崇道及其三子並坐死，親友皆決杖流貶。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered Xu to investigate the case. Xu wished to wield authority on his own authority, so he arrested and imprisoned several dozen of Chongdao's kin and associates, all put to extreme torture, and only then fabricated their guilt. Chongdao and his three sons were all sentenced to death; friends and relatives were all beaten with the rod and exiled or demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong ordered Xu to investigate the case. Xu wished to wield authority on his own, so he arrested and imprisoned several dozen of Chongdao's kin and associates, all put to extreme torture, and only then fabricated their guilt. Chongdao and his three sons were all sentenced to death; friends and relatives were all beaten with the rod and exiled or demoted.

sentences.zh: 時得罪多是知名之士，四海冤之。

translations.literal: At that time those convicted were mostly men of renown, and the realm regarded it as an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: At that time those convicted were mostly men of renown, and the realm regarded it as an injustice.

sentences.zh: 旭又與御史大夫李傑不協，遞相糾訐，傑竟坐左遷衢州刺史。

translations.literal: Xu also fell out with Censor-in-Chief Li Jie and they mutually impeached each other. Jie was in the end demoted to Prefect of Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu also fell out with Censor-in-Chief Li Jie and they mutually impeached each other. Jie was in the end demoted to Prefect of Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 旭既得志，擅行威福，由是朝廷畏而鄙之。

translations.literal: Once Xu had gotten his way, he acted with arbitrary power and favor, and thereafter the court both feared and despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xu had gotten his way, he acted with arbitrary power and favor, and thereafter the court both feared and despised him.

sentences.zh: 俄以贓罪黜爲龍川尉，憤恚而死，甚爲時之所快。

translations.literal: Before long, for the crime of corruption he was dismissed to serve as Sheriff of Longchuan. He died of indignation and resentment, to the great satisfaction of his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, for the crime of corruption he was dismissed to serve as Sheriff of Longchuan. He died of indignation and resentment, to the great satisfaction of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 戴胄戴胄，字玄胤，相州安陽人也。

translations.literal: Dai Zhou, styled Xuanyin, was a native of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhou, styled Xuanyin, was a native of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性貞正，有干局。

translations.literal: His character was upright and correct, and he possessed practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and capable by nature, he had a talent for practical administration.

sentences.zh: 明習律令，尤曉文簿。

translations.literal: He was well versed in statutes and ordinances and especially understood written records.
translations.idiomatic: He was well versed in law and especially skilled at reading official documents.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，爲門下錄事，納言蘇威、黃門侍郎裴矩甚禮之。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye of Sui he served as Recorder in the Chancellery. Su Wei, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Pei Ju, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, greatly honored him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui Daye era he served as Recorder in the Chancellery. Su Wei, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Pei Ju, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 越王侗以爲給事郎。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Tong appointed him Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Tong appointed him Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 王世充將篡侗位，胄言於世充曰：「君臣之分，情均父子，理須同其休戚，勖以終始。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong was about to usurp Tong's throne, Zhou said to Shichong: "The distinction between ruler and minister is in feeling equal to that between father and son. In principle one must share their joys and sorrows and encourage them from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong was about to usurp Tong's throne, Zhou said to him, "The bond between ruler and minister should be as close as that between father and son. In principle one must share their joys and sorrows and stand by them from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 明公以文武之才，當社稷之寄，與存與亡，在於今日。

translations.literal: Your Excellency, with civil and military talent, bears the charge of the state. Whether it survives or perishes depends on this day.
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency, with your civil and military talents, bear the charge of the state. Whether it survives or perishes depends on what you do today.

sentences.zh: 所願推誠王室，擬跡伊、周，使國有泰山之安，家傳代祿之盛，則率土之濱，莫不幸甚。」

translations.literal: What I wish is that you devote yourself sincerely to the royal house, model yourself on Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, and make the state secure as Mount Tai and your family pass down generations of emolument — then all within the realm would be supremely fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: What I wish is that you devote yourself sincerely to the royal house, take Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou as your models, and make the state secure as Mount Tai and your family pass down generations of emolument — then all within the realm would be supremely fortunate.

sentences.zh: 世充詭辭稱善，勞而遣之。

translations.literal: Shichong spoke deceptively in praise and, after expressing appreciation, sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong answered with deceptive praise and, after expressing appreciation, dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 世充後逼越王加其九錫，胄又抗言切諫。

translations.literal: Later Shichong forced the Prince of Yue to bestow the Nine Bestowals upon him, and Zhou again spoke out in forceful remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shichong forced the Prince of Yue to bestow the Nine Bestowals upon him, and Zhou again remonstrated forcefully.

sentences.zh: 世充不納，由是出爲鄭州長史，令與兄子行本鎮武牢。

translations.literal: Shichong did not accept his counsel. For this reason Zhou was sent out as Chief Administrator of Zheng Prefecture and ordered to garrison Wulao together with his elder brother's son Xingben.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong did not accept his counsel. Zhou was therefore sent out as Chief Administrator of Zheng Prefecture and ordered to garrison Wulao together with his elder brother's son Xingben.

sentences.zh: 太宗克武牢而得之，引爲秦府士曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Taizong captured Wulao and took him, he was appointed Army Staff Officer in the Prince of Qin's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong captured Wulao and took him prisoner, he appointed him Army Staff Officer in the Prince of Qin's Office.

sentences.zh: 及即位，除兵部郎中，封武昌縣男。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne, Zhou was appointed Director in the Ministry of War and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuchang County.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ascended the throne, he appointed Zhou Director in the Ministry of War and enfeoffed him as Baron of Wuchang County.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時吏部尚書長孫無忌嘗被召，不解佩刀入東上閣。

translations.literal: At that time Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Personnel, was once summoned and entered the Eastern Upper Hall without removing the sword at his belt.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Personnel, was once summoned and entered the Eastern Upper Hall without removing the sword at his belt.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射封德彝議以監門校尉不覺，罪當死；

translations.literal: Feng Deyi, Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, proposed that the gate-guard captain who had failed to notice should be punished with death;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Deyi, Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, proposed that the gate-guard captain who had failed to notice should be punished with death;

sentences.zh: 無忌誤帶入，罰銅二十斤。

translations.literal: Wuji, for mistakenly bringing it in, should be fined twenty jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji, for mistakenly bringing it in, should be fined twenty jin of copper.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 胄駁曰：「校尉不覺與無忌帶入，同爲誤耳。

translations.literal: Zhou objected: "The captain's failure to notice and Wuji's bringing it in are both mistakes alike.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou objected, "The captain's failure to notice and Wuji's bringing it in are both mistakes alike.

sentences.zh: 臣子之於尊極，不得稱誤，准律云：『供御湯藥、飲食、舟船，誤不知者，皆死。』

translations.literal: Before one's sovereign a subject may not plead mistake. According to the law: 'For supplying the imperial bath, medicines, food, drink, or boats — if through mistake one did not know, all are punishable by death.
translations.idiomatic: Before one's sovereign a subject may not plead mistake. According to the law, 'For supplying the imperial bath, medicines, food, drink, or boats — if through mistake one did not know, all are punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 陛下若錄其功，非憲司所決；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty records his merit, that is not for the judicial authorities to decide;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty records his merit, that is not for the judicial authorities to decide;

sentences.zh: 若當據法，罰銅未爲得衷。」

translations.literal: if one must follow the law, a copper fine is not the proper middle course.
translations.idiomatic: if one must follow the law, a copper fine is not the proper middle course.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「法者，非朕一人之法，乃天下之法也。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Law is not my law alone — it is the law of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Law is not my law alone — it is the law of the realm.

sentences.zh: 何得以無忌國之親戚，便欲阿之？」

translations.literal: How can you, because Wuji is a kinsman of the state, wish to show favor to him?"
translations.idiomatic: How can you, because Wuji is a kinsman of the state, wish to show favor to him?"

sentences.zh: 更令定議。

translations.literal: He ordered the matter decided again.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the matter decided again.

sentences.zh: 德彝執議如初，太宗將從其議，胄又曰：「校尉緣無忌以致罪，於法當輕。

translations.literal: Deyi held to his original proposal. Taizong was about to follow it when Zhou again said: "The captain incurred guilt because of Wuji; by law the penalty should be lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi held to his original proposal. Taizong was about to follow it when Zhou again said, "The captain incurred guilt because of Wuji; by law the penalty should be lighter.

sentences.zh: 若論其誤，則爲情一也，而生死頓殊，敢以固請。」

translations.literal: If one considers the mistake, the circumstances are the same, yet life and death differ utterly. I venture to press my request firmly.
translations.idiomatic: If one considers the mistake, the circumstances are the same, yet life and death would differ utterly. I venture to press my request firmly.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，竟免校尉之死。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and in the end spared the captain from death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and in the end spared the captain from death.

sentences.zh: 於時朝廷盛開選舉，或有詐偽資廕者，帝令其自首，不首者罪至於死。

translations.literal: At that time the court was vigorously conducting selections and appointments. Some had falsely claimed inherited privilege. The emperor ordered them to confess; those who did not would be guilty of a capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was vigorously conducting selections and appointments. Some had falsely claimed inherited privilege. The emperor ordered them to confess; those who did not would be guilty of a capital crime.

sentences.zh: 俄有詐偽者事洩，胄據法斷流以奏之。

translations.literal: Before long a case of fraud was exposed. Zhou, following the law, sentenced exile and submitted the decision.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a case of fraud was exposed. Zhou, following the law, sentenced the offender to exile and submitted the decision.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕下敕不首者死，今斷從流，是示天下以不信。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I issued an edict that those who did not confess should die. Now you sentence exile — this shows the realm that I am not to be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I issued an edict that those who did not confess should die. Now you sentence exile — this shows the realm that I am not to be trusted.

sentences.zh: 卿欲賣獄乎？」

translations.literal: Do you wish to sell judgments?
translations.idiomatic: Do you wish to sell judgments?

sentences.zh: 胄曰：「陛下當即殺之，非臣所及。

translations.literal: Zhou said: "If Your Majesty executes him at once, that is beyond my reach.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou said, "If Your Majesty executes him at once, that is beyond my reach.

sentences.zh: 既付所司，臣不敢虧法。」

translations.literal: Since the case has been handed to the authorities, I dare not violate the law."
translations.idiomatic: Since the case has been handed to the authorities, I dare not violate the law."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿自守法，而令我失信邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You keep the law yourself, yet make me break faith?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You keep the law yourself, yet make me break faith?"

sentences.zh: 胄曰：「法者，國家所以布大信於天下；

translations.literal: Zhou said: "Law is how the state establishes great trust with the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou said, "Law is how the state establishes great trust with the realm;

sentences.zh: 言者，當時喜怒之所發耳。

translations.literal: words are merely what anger or joy of the moment give rise to.
translations.idiomatic: words are merely what anger or joy of the moment give rise to.

sentences.zh: 陛下發一朝之忿而許殺之，既知不可而置之於法，此乃忍小忿而存大信也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, moved by a moment's anger, promised death; now knowing it cannot be done, you place the matter within the law. This is restraining a small anger to preserve great trust.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, moved by a moment's anger, promised death; now knowing it cannot be done, you place the matter within the law. This is restraining a small anger to preserve great trust.

sentences.zh: 若順忿違信，臣竊爲陛下惜之。」

translations.literal: If you follow anger and violate trust, I privately regret this for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: If you follow anger and violate trust, I privately regret this for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「法有所失，公能正之，朕何憂也！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When the law errs, you can set it right — what have I to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When the law errs, you can set it right — what have I to worry about!"

sentences.zh: 胄前後犯顏執法多此類。

translations.literal: Zhou's bold remonstrance and firm adherence to law were often of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou often remonstrated boldly and held firm to the law in this way.

sentences.zh: 所論刑獄，皆事無冤濫，隨方指扌適，言如泉湧。

translations.literal: In criminal cases he discussed, there were never wrongful convictions; he adapted his arguments to each situation and his words flowed like a spring.
translations.idiomatic: In the criminal cases he discussed there were never wrongful convictions; he adapted his arguments to each situation and his words flowed like a spring.

sentences.zh: 其年，轉尚書右丞，尋遷左丞。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and soon after promoted to Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was transferred to Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and soon after promoted to Left Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 先是，每歲水旱，皆以正倉出給，無倉之處，就食他州，百姓多致飢乏。

translations.literal: Previously, each year during flood or drought grain was issued from the principal granaries. Where there were no granaries, people went to other prefectures for food, and the common people often suffered hunger and want.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, each year during flood or drought grain was issued from the principal granaries. Where there were no granaries, people went to other prefectures for food, and the common people often suffered hunger and want.

sentences.zh: 二年，胄上言：「水旱凶災，前聖之所不免。

translations.literal: In the second year Zhou submitted a memorial: "Flood, drought, and calamity are what even the sage rulers of old could not avoid.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Zhou submitted a memorial, "Flood, drought, and calamity are what even the sage rulers of old could not avoid.

sentences.zh: 國無九年儲蓄，禮經之所明誡。

translations.literal: A state without nine years' reserves is what the Book of Rites clearly warns against.
translations.idiomatic: A state without nine years' reserves is what the Book of Rites clearly warns against.

sentences.zh: 今喪亂已後，戸口凋殘，每歲納租，未實倉稟。

translations.literal: Now after the chaos of war, households are depleted and ruined. Each year's tax payments do not actually fill the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Now after the chaos of war, households are depleted and ruined. Each year's tax payments do not actually fill the granaries.

sentences.zh: 隨即出給，才供當年，若有凶災，將何賑恤？

translations.literal: It is immediately issued out and barely suffices for the current year. If calamity strikes, with what will we provide relief?
translations.idiomatic: It is immediately issued out and barely suffices for the current year. If calamity strikes, with what will we provide relief?

sentences.zh: 故隋開皇立制，天下之人，節級輸粟，名爲社倉，終文皇代，得無饑饉。

translations.literal: Therefore in Kaihuang of Sui a system was established: people throughout the realm paid grain by graduated rates, called community granaries. Through the era of Emperor Wen there was no famine.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in the Sui Kaihuang era a system was established: people throughout the realm paid grain by graduated rates into what were called community granaries. Through the era of Emperor Wen there was no famine.

sentences.zh: 及大業中年，國用不足，並取社倉之物以充官費，故至末途，無以支給。

translations.literal: By the middle of Daye, state expenses were insufficient and the goods of the community granaries were all taken to meet official costs. Therefore at the end there was nothing with which to provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: By the middle of the Daye era, state expenses were insufficient and the goods of the community granaries were all taken to meet official costs. Therefore at the end there was nothing with which to provide relief.

sentences.zh: 自王公已下，爰及眾庶，計所墾田稼穡頃畝，每至秋熟，准其苗以理勸課，盡令出粟。

translations.literal: From princes and dukes down to the common people, calculating the acreage of cultivated fields and crops, each autumn at harvest, assessing according to the seedlings and encouraging payment by rule, all should be made to contribute grain.
translations.idiomatic: From princes and dukes down to the common people, calculating the acreage of cultivated fields and crops, each autumn at harvest, assessing according to the seedlings and encouraging payment by rule, all should be made to contribute grain.

sentences.zh: 稻麥之鄕，亦同此稅，各納所在，立爲義倉。」

translations.literal: In districts of rice and wheat the same tax applies. Each pays where he resides, and community relief granaries are established.
translations.idiomatic: In districts of rice and wheat the same tax applies. Each pays where he resides, and community relief granaries are established.

sentences.zh: 太宗從其議。

translations.literal: Taizong followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong followed his proposal.

sentences.zh: 以其家貧，齎錢十萬。

translations.literal: Because his family was poor, he was given one hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Because his family was poor, the emperor gave him one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 時尚書左僕射蕭瑀免官，僕射封德彝又卒，太宗謂胄曰：「尚書省天下綱維，百司所稟，若一事有失，天下必有受其弊者。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Yu, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was dismissed from office, and Vice Director Feng Deyi also died. Taizong said to Zhou: "The Imperial Secretariat is the backbone of the realm, from which all offices receive direction. If one matter goes wrong, the realm will surely suffer from it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Yu, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was dismissed from office, and Vice Director Feng Deyi also died. Taizong said to Zhou, "The Imperial Secretariat is the backbone of the realm, from which all offices receive direction. If one matter goes wrong, the realm will surely suffer from it.

sentences.zh: 今以令、僕系之於卿，當稱朕所望也。」

translations.literal: Now I entrust the duties of Director and Vice Director to you — you should live up to what I expect.
translations.idiomatic: Now I entrust the duties of Director and Vice Director to you — you should live up to what I expect.

sentences.zh: 胄性明敏，達於從政，處斷明速。

translations.literal: Zhou's nature was bright and quick; he was adept at governance and decided matters with clarity and speed.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and quick by nature, Zhou was adept at governance and decided matters with clarity and speed.

sentences.zh: 議者以爲左右丞稱職，武德已來，一人而已。

translations.literal: Commentators held that among left and right assistant directors who fulfilled their duties, since Wude there had been only one such man.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that among left and right assistant directors who fulfilled their duties, since the Wude era there had been only one such man.

sentences.zh: 又領諫議大夫，令與魏徵更日供奉。

translations.literal: He also held the post of Remonstrating Adviser and was ordered to attend the emperor on alternate days with Wei Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also held the post of Remonstrating Adviser and was ordered to attend the emperor on alternate days with Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 三年，進拜民部尚書，兼檢校太子左庶子。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Minister of Revenue and concurrently appointed Acting Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Minister of Revenue and concurrently appointed Acting Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 先是，右僕射杜如晦專掌選舉，臨終請以選事委胄，由是詔令兼攝吏部尚書，其民部、庶子、諫議並如故。

translations.literal: Previously, Du Ruhui, Right Vice Director, had sole charge of selections and appointments. On his deathbed he requested that selection affairs be entrusted to Zhou. For this reason an edict ordered Zhou to concurrently administer the Ministry of Personnel; his posts as Minister of Revenue, Assistant to the Heir Apparent, and Remonstrating Adviser remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Du Ruhui, Right Vice Director, had sole charge of selections and appointments. On his deathbed he requested that selection affairs be entrusted to Zhou. An edict therefore ordered Zhou to concurrently administer the Ministry of Personnel; his posts as Minister of Revenue, Assistant to the Heir Apparent, and Remonstrating Adviser remained as before.

sentences.zh: 胄雖有干局，而無學術。

translations.literal: Although Zhou had practical ability, he lacked scholarly learning.
translations.idiomatic: Although Zhou had practical ability, he lacked scholarly learning.

sentences.zh: 居吏部，抑文雅而獎法吏，甚爲時論所譏。

translations.literal: While in the Ministry of Personnel he suppressed men of letters and favored legal officials, and was much ridiculed in contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: While in the Ministry of Personnel he suppressed men of letters and favored legal officials, and was much ridiculed in contemporary opinion.

sentences.zh: 四年，罷吏部尚書，以本官參預朝政，尋進爵爲郡公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was removed as Minister of Personnel, retained his original post to participate in court governance, and soon after was advanced to Grand Duke of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was removed as Minister of Personnel, retained his original post to participate in court governance, and soon after was advanced to Grand Duke of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 五年，太宗將修復洛陽宮，胄上表諫曰：

translations.literal: In the fifth year Taizong was about to restore the Luoyang palace. Zhou submitted a memorial remonstrating:
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Taizong was about to restore the Luoyang palace. Zhou submitted a memorial remonstrating:

sentences.zh: 陛下當百王之弊，屬暴隋之後，拯餘燼於塗炭，救遺黎於倒懸。

translations.literal: Your Majesty faces the accumulated evils of a hundred kings and comes after the tyrannical Sui, rescuing embers from the coals and saving the surviving people from hanging upside down.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty faces the accumulated evils of a hundred kings and comes after the tyrannical Sui, rescuing embers from the coals and saving the surviving people from hanging upside down.

sentences.zh: 遠至邇安，率土清謐，大功大德，豈臣之所稱讚。

translations.literal: The distant have come and the near are at peace; the realm is tranquil. Such great merit and virtue — how could a subject like me presume to praise them?
translations.idiomatic: The distant have come and the near are at peace; the realm is tranquil. Such great merit and virtue — how could a subject like me presume to praise them?

sentences.zh: 臣誠小人，才識非遠，唯知耳目之近，不達長久之策，敢竭區區之誠，論臣職司之事。

translations.literal: I am truly a petty man; my talent and insight do not reach far. I know only what is before my eyes and do not grasp long-term strategy. I venture to pour forth my humble sincerity and discuss matters within my official charge.
translations.idiomatic: I am truly a petty man; my talent and insight do not reach far. I know only what is before my eyes and do not grasp long-term strategy. I venture to pour forth my humble sincerity and discuss matters within my official charge.

sentences.zh: 比見關中、河外，盡置軍團，富室強丁，並從戎旅。

translations.literal: Recently I have seen that within the passes and beyond the Yellow River, army regiments have been established everywhere. Wealthy households and strong young men have all joined the military.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I have seen that within the passes and beyond the Yellow River, army regiments have been established everywhere. Wealthy households and strong young men have all joined the military.

sentences.zh: 重以九成作役，余丁向盡，去京二千里內，先配司農將作。

translations.literal: Added to this is labor on the Jiucheng palace. The remaining laborers are nearly exhausted. Within two thousand li of the capital, men are first assigned to the Court of the National Granaries and the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this is labor on the Jiucheng palace. The remaining laborers are nearly exhausted. Within two thousand li of the capital, men are first assigned to the Court of the National Granaries and the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 假有遺余，勢何足紀？

translations.literal: Even if any remain, how could their number be worth recording?
translations.idiomatic: Even if any remain, how could their number be worth recording?

sentences.zh: 亂離甫爾，戸口單弱，一人就役，舉家便廢。

translations.literal: Disorder and separation have only just ended; households are few and weak. When one man enters service, the whole family is ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Disorder and separation have only just ended; households are few and weak. When one man enters service, the whole family is ruined.

sentences.zh: 入軍者督其戎仗，從役者責其餱糧，盡室經營，多不能濟。

translations.literal: Those entering the army are pressed for weapons and gear; those on labor service are charged for dry rations. Whole households struggle to manage, and many cannot make ends meet.
translations.idiomatic: Those entering the army are pressed for weapons and gear; those on labor service are charged for dry rations. Whole households struggle to manage, and many cannot make ends meet.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚慮，恐致怨嗟。

translations.literal: In my foolish thinking, I fear this will provoke resentment and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: In my foolish thinking, I fear this will provoke resentment and sighing.

sentences.zh: 七月已來，霖潦過度，河南、河北，厥田洿下，時豐歲稔，猶未可量。

translations.literal: Since the seventh month excessive rains have fallen. In Henan and Hebei the fields are low and waterlogged. Even in a year of timely abundance and good harvest, the outcome cannot yet be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Since the seventh month excessive rains have fallen. In Henan and Hebei the fields are low and waterlogged. Even in a year of timely abundance and good harvest, the outcome cannot yet be measured.

sentences.zh: 加以軍國所須，皆資府庫，布絹所出，歲過百萬。

translations.literal: Added to this, what the army and state require all depends on the treasuries. The cloth and silk issued exceeds one million each year.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this, what the army and state require all depends on the treasuries. The cloth and silk issued exceeds one million each year.

sentences.zh: 丁既役盡，賦調不減，費用不止，帑藏其虛。

translations.literal: Laborers are already exhausted, yet taxes and levies are not reduced; expenses do not cease, and the treasuries are emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers are already exhausted, yet taxes and levies are not reduced; expenses do not cease, and the treasuries are emptied.

sentences.zh: 且洛陽宮殿，足蔽風雨，數年功畢，亦謂非晩。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Luoyang palace is sufficient to shelter from wind and rain. Completing the work over several years would also not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Luoyang palace is sufficient to shelter from wind and rain. Completing the work over several years would also not be too late.

sentences.zh: 若頓修營，恐傷勞擾。

translations.literal: If construction is rushed, I fear it will harm the people through forced labor and disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: If construction is rushed, I fear it will harm the people through forced labor and disturbance.

sentences.zh: 太宗甚嘉之，因謂侍臣曰：「戴胄於我無骨肉之親，但以忠直勵行，情深體國，事有機要，無不以聞。

translations.literal: Taizong greatly praised this and then told his attending officials: "Dai Zhou has no kinship with me by blood, yet through loyal uprightness he urges himself on. His feeling for the state runs deep. Whenever matters are critical, he withholds nothing from me.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong greatly praised this and then told his attending officials, "Dai Zhou has no kinship with me by blood, yet through loyal uprightness he urges himself on. His feeling for the state runs deep. Whenever matters are critical, he withholds nothing from me.

sentences.zh: 所進官爵，以酬厥誠耳。」

translations.literal: The offices and titles I have advanced to him are merely to repay his sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: The offices and titles I have advanced to him are merely to repay his sincerity.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，太宗爲之舉哀，廢朝三日。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died. Taizong mourned for him and suspended court for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died. Taizong mourned for him and suspended court for three days.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書右僕射，追封道國公，謚曰忠，詔虞世南撰爲碑文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Daoguo, with the posthumous title Zhong. An edict ordered Yu Shinan to compose his epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Daoguo, with the posthumous title Zhong. An edict ordered Yu Shinan to compose his epitaph.

sentences.zh: 又以胄宅宇弊陋，祭享無所，令有司特爲造廟。

translations.literal: Because Zhou's residence was dilapidated and there was no place for sacrifices, the authorities were ordered specially to build a temple for him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhou's residence was dilapidated and there was no place for sacrifices, the authorities were ordered specially to build a temple for him.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡、魏徵並美胄才用，俱與之親善，及胄卒後，嘗見其游處之地，數爲之流涕。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling and Wei Zheng both admired Zhou's talent and ability and were both close friends with him. After Zhou died, whenever they saw places where he had lived and visited, they often wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and Wei Zheng both admired Zhou's talent and ability and were both close friends with him. After Zhou died, whenever they saw places where he had lived and visited, they often wept for him.

sentences.zh: 胄無子，以兄子至德爲後。

translations.literal: Zhou had no son and made his elder brother's son Zhiede his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had no son and made his elder brother's son Zhiede his heir.

sentences.zh: 胄兄子 至德至德，乾封中累遷西台侍郎、同東西台三品。

translations.literal: Zhou's elder brother's son Zhiede, during Qianfeng, was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Western Terrace and Associate of the Third Rank of the Eastern and Western Terraces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's elder brother's son Zhiede, during the Qianfeng era, was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Western Terrace and Associate of the Third Rank of the Eastern and Western Terraces.

sentences.zh: 尋轉戸部尚書，依舊知政事。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to Minister of Revenue and continued to participate in governance as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was transferred to Minister of Revenue and continued to participate in governance as before.

sentences.zh: 父子十數年間相繼爲尚書，預知國政，時以爲榮。

translations.literal: Over more than ten years father and son successively served as Minister and participated in state affairs — at the time this was considered an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than ten years uncle and nephew successively served as Minister and participated in state affairs — at the time this was considered an honor.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，高宗爲飛白書以賜侍臣，賜至德曰「泛洪源，俟舟楫」；

translations.literal: During Xianheng, Emperor Gaozong wrote in flying-white script to bestow on attending ministers. To Zhiede he gave: "Cross the great source and await boat and oar";
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianheng era, Emperor Gaozong wrote in flying-white script to bestow on attending ministers. To Zhiede he gave, "Cross the great source and await boat and oar";

sentences.zh: 賜郝處俊曰「飛九霄，假六翮」；

translations.literal: to Hao Chujun: "Soar to the nine heavens, borrow six pinions";
translations.idiomatic: to Hao Chujun, "Soar to the nine heavens, borrow six pinions";

sentences.zh: 賜李敬玄曰「資啟沃，罄丹誠」；

translations.literal: to Li Jingxuan: "Supply nourishing counsel, pour forth red sincerity";
translations.idiomatic: to Li Jingxuan, "Supply nourishing counsel, pour forth red sincerity";

sentences.zh: 又賜中書侍郎崔知悌曰「竭忠節，贊皇猷」，其辭皆有興比。

translations.literal: and to Cui Zhi, Vice Director of the Central Secretariat: "Exhaust loyal integrity, assist the imperial design." All the phrases contained allegorical comparisons.
translations.idiomatic: and to Cui Zhi, Vice Director of the Central Secretariat, "Exhaust loyal integrity, assist the imperial design." All the phrases contained allegorical comparisons.

sentences.zh: 俄遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時劉仁軌爲左僕射，每遇申訴冤滯者，輒美言許之；

translations.literal: At that time Liu Ren'gui was Left Vice Director. Whenever someone appealed a grievance or delay in justice, he would readily promise relief in fine words;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Ren'gui was Left Vice Director. Whenever someone appealed a grievance or delay in justice, he would readily promise relief in fine words;

sentences.zh: 而至德先據理難詰，未嘗與奪，若有理者，密爲奏之，終不顯己之斷決，由是時譽歸於仁軌。

translations.literal: Zhiede, by contrast, first examined the reasoning and questioned closely, never deciding on the spot. If the case had merit, he secretly submitted a memorial. He never displayed his own judgment, and for this reason contemporary reputation went to Ren'gui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiede, by contrast, first examined the reasoning and questioned closely, never deciding on the spot. If the case had merit, he secretly submitted a memorial. He never displayed his own judgment, and for this reason contemporary reputation went to Ren'gui.

sentences.zh: 或以問至德，答曰：「夫慶賞刑罪，人主之權柄，凡爲人臣，豈得與人主爭權柄哉！」

translations.literal: When someone asked Zhiede about this, he replied: "Rewards, punishments, and penalties are the sovereign's prerogative. As a subject, how can one contend with the sovereign for prerogative!
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked Zhiede about this, he replied, "Rewards, punishments, and penalties are the sovereign's prerogative. As a subject, how can one contend with the sovereign for prerogative!

sentences.zh: 其慎密如此。

translations.literal: Such was his caution and discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his caution and discretion.

sentences.zh: 後高宗知而深嘆美之。

translations.literal: Later, when Emperor Gaozong learned of this, he deeply sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Gaozong learned of this, he deeply sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳四年薨，輟朝三日，使百官以次赴宅哭之，贈開府儀同三司、并州大都督，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yifeng he died. Court was suspended for three days and all officials were sent in turn to his residence to mourn. He was posthumously appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the rank of the Three Excellencies and Grand Protector General of Bing Prefecture, with the posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yifeng he died. Court was suspended for three days and all officials were sent in turn to his residence to mourn. He was posthumously appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the rank of the Three Excellencies and Grand Protector General of Bing Prefecture, with the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 岑文本岑文本，字景仁，南陽棘陽人。

translations.literal: Cen Wenben Cen Wenben, styled Jingren, was a native of Jiyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Wenben, styled Jingren, was a native of Jiyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖善方，仕蕭察吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shanfang served Xiao Cha as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shanfang had served Xiao Cha as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 父之象，隋末爲邯鄲令，嘗被人所訟，理不得申。

translations.literal: His father Zhixiang, in the late Sui served as magistrate of Handan; he was once sued by someone and could not vindicate his case.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhixiang, in the late Sui dynasty, served as magistrate of Handan. He was once brought to court by an accuser and could not clear himself.

sentences.zh: 文本性沈敏，有姿儀，博考經史，多所貫綜，美談論，善屬文。

translations.literal: Wenben's nature was deep and quick; he had fine bearing, broadly examined the classics and histories with wide synthesis, excelled in discussion, and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben was deep and quick-witted by nature, with a dignified bearing. He studied the classics and histories broadly and mastered many subjects, excelled in conversation, and wrote with great skill.

sentences.zh: 時年十四，詣司隸稱冤，辭情慨切，召對明辯，眾頗異之。

translations.literal: At the time he was fourteen. He went to the Director of Retainers to plead injustice; his words were impassioned and urgent. Summoned for audience, he argued clearly and discerningly, and many found this remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he went before the Director of Retainers to plead his father's case. His words were impassioned, and when summoned for audience he argued with clarity and force. Many were struck by it.

sentences.zh: 試令作《蓮花賦》，下筆便成，屬意甚佳，合台莫不歎賞。

translations.literal: They tested him by having him compose the "Rhapsody on the Lotus"; his brush formed it at once, its intent very fine, and everyone at the tribunal sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: They tested him by asking for a composition of the 《Lotus Rhapsody》. He finished it at a stroke, with excellent conception, and everyone present sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 其父冤雪，由是知名。

translations.literal: His father's wrong was cleared, and from this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: His father's injustice was redressed, and from that time his name became known.

sentences.zh: 其後，郡舉秀才，以時亂不應。

translations.literal: Afterward the commandery recommended him as xiucai, but because of the turmoil of the times he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Later the commandery recommended him as a xiucai, but he declined to accept because of the disorder of the age.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑僭號於荊州，召署中書侍郎，專典文翰。

translations.literal: Xiao Xian usurped the title at Jingzhou, summoned him, and appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat, exclusively in charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xian declared himself emperor at Jingzhou, he summoned Wenben and appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat, putting him solely in charge of official writing.

sentences.zh: 及河間王孝恭定荊州，軍中將士咸欲大掠，文本進説孝恭曰：「自隋室無道，群雄鼎沸，四海延頸以望真主。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Hejian, Li Xiaogong, pacified Jingzhou, the officers and soldiers in the army all wished to plunder on a great scale. Wenben went forward to advise Xiaogong, saying: "Since the Sui house was without the Way, heroes seethed like a cauldron, and throughout the four seas men stretched their necks awaiting a true lord.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Hejian, Li Xiaogong, pacified Jingzhou, the officers and soldiers all wanted to loot the city on a grand scale. Wenben went to advise Xiaogong, saying, "Since the Sui house lost the Way, rival powers have seethed like a boiling cauldron, and throughout the realm men have longed for a true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 今蕭氏君臣、江陵父老，決計歸降者，實望去危就安耳。

translations.literal: Now the lord and ministers of the Xiao clan and the elders of Jiangling who resolved to surrender truly wished only to leave danger and reach safety.
translations.idiomatic: The lord and ministers of the Xiao house and the elders of Jiangling who have resolved to surrender have done so only because they wished to escape danger and find safety.

sentences.zh: 王必欲縱兵虜掠，誠非鄙州來蘇之意，亦恐江、嶺以南，向化之心沮矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Highness must let troops loose to capture and plunder, it truly is not the meaning of this province's 'return to life,' and I also fear that south of the Yangzi and the Ling ranges the hearts turning toward civilization will be dampened."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness insists on letting the army plunder, that is truly not what this province meant by 'returning to life,' and I fear it will also discourage those south of the Yangzi and the Ling ranges who are turning toward allegiance."

sentences.zh: 孝恭稱善，遂止之。

translations.literal: Xiaogong praised this and thereupon stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong approved and stopped them.

sentences.zh: 署文本荊州別駕。

translations.literal: He appointed Wenben Vice Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Wenben Vice Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝恭進擊輔公祏，召典軍書，復署行台考功郎中。

translations.literal: When Xiaogong advanced to attack Fu Gongshi, he summoned Wenben to manage military documents and again appointed him Evaluation Section Director of the Mobile Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaogong marched against Fu Gongshi, he summoned Wenben to manage military documents and again appointed him Evaluation Section Director of the field secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，除秘書郎，兼直中書省。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was appointed Secretary and concurrently served in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he was appointed Secretary and concurrently served on duty in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遇太宗行藉田之禮，文本上《藉田頌》。

translations.literal: When Taizong performed the ceremonial plowing rites, Wenben submitted the "Ode on Ceremonial Ploughing."
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong performed the ceremonial plowing rites, Wenben submitted the 《Ode on Ceremonial Ploughing》.

sentences.zh: 及元日臨軒宴百僚，文本復上《三元頌》，其辭甚美。

translations.literal: When on New Year's Day Taizong held court and feasted the hundred officials, Wenben again submitted the "Ode on the Three Primes," and its language was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, when Taizong held court and feasted the hundred officials, Wenben again submitted the 《Ode on the Three Primes》, and its wording was superb.

sentences.zh: 文本才名既著，李靖復稱薦之，擢拜中書舍人，漸蒙親顧。

translations.literal: Wenben's talent and fame already prominent, Li Jing again praised and recommended him; he was promoted and appointed Secretariat Drafter and gradually received personal favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben's talent and reputation were already well known. Li Jing recommended him again, and he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter, gradually winning the emperor's personal regard.

sentences.zh: 初，武德中詔誥及軍國大事，文皆出於顏師古。

translations.literal: Initially, during Wude, edicts and major military and state affairs all had their documents come from Yan Shigu.
translations.idiomatic: At first, during the Wude era, the drafting of edicts and documents on major military and state affairs had all been done by Yan Shigu.

sentences.zh: 至是，文本所草詔誥。

translations.literal: From this point, the edicts Wenben drafted.
translations.idiomatic: From this point on, the edicts were drafted by Wenben.

sentences.zh: 或眾務繁湊，即命書僮六七人隨口並寫，須臾悉成，亦殆盡其妙。

translations.literal: When many tasks piled up densely, he would order six or seven copy boys to write simultaneously as he dictated; in a moment all were finished, also nearly exhausting his marvelous skill.
translations.idiomatic: When business piled up, he would have six or seven copy boys write at once as he dictated, and in a moment everything was finished—a feat that nearly exhausted the limits of his art.

sentences.zh: 時中書侍郎顏師古以譴免職，頃之，溫彥博奏曰：「師古諳練時事，長於文法，時無及者，冀蒙復用。」

translations.literal: At the time Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Shigu was dismissed through reprimand. Soon Wen Yanbo memorialized, saying: "Shigu is practiced in current affairs and excels in literary regulations; none now surpass him. I hope he may be re-employed."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Shigu had been dismissed after a reprimand. Before long Wen Yanbo memorialized, saying, "Shigu is thoroughly versed in current affairs and excels in literary form; no one today equals him. I hope he may be reappointed."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「我自舉一人，公勿憂也。」
