translations.literal: Taizong said: "I shall myself select one man—you need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "I shall choose someone myself. You need not worry."

sentences.zh: 於是以文本爲中書侍郎，專典機密。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wenben was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, exclusively handling classified matters.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wenben was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and put solely in charge of confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 又先與令狐德棻撰《周史》，其史論多出於文本。

translations.literal: He had also earlier with Linghu Defen compiled the History of the Zhou, and most of its historical judgments came from Wenben.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier compiled the 《History of the Zhou》 with Linghu Defen, and most of its historical judgments were written by Wenben.

sentences.zh: 至十年史成，封江陵縣子。

translations.literal: By the tenth year the history was completed, and he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the history was completed, and he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從至洛陽宮，會谷、洛泛溢，文本上封事曰：

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he accompanied Taizong to Luoyang Palace. The Yi and Luo rivers overflowed, and Wenben submitted a sealed memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he accompanied Taizong to Luoyang Palace. When the Yi and Luo rivers flooded, Wenben submitted a sealed memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞創撥亂之業，其功既難；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that founding an enterprise amid chaos is already difficult in achievement;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to found an enterprise amid chaos is already a hard achievement;

sentences.zh: 守已成之基，其道不易。

translations.literal: preserving an established foundation—its Way is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: and to preserve an established foundation is no easy task.

sentences.zh: 故居安思危，所以定其業也；

translations.literal: Therefore dwelling in peace yet thinking of peril is how one settles one's enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore to dwell in security yet think of danger is how one secures one's enterprise;

sentences.zh: 有始有卒，所以隆其基也。

translations.literal: having a beginning and an end is how one elevates one's foundation.
translations.idiomatic: and to carry a task from beginning to end is how one strengthens its foundation.

sentences.zh: 今雖億兆乂安，方隅寧謐，既承喪亂之後，又接凋弊之餘，戸口減損尚多，田疇墾闢猶少。

translations.literal: Though now the myriad multitudes are governed in peace and the regions are tranquil and quiet, having succeeded the age of turmoil and meeting the aftermath of exhaustion, household registers still show much reduction and reclaimed fields remain few.
translations.idiomatic: Though the myriad people are now governed in peace and the regions are tranquil, we have succeeded an age of turmoil and inherited a land still exhausted. Household registers remain greatly reduced, and reclaimed fields are still few.

sentences.zh: 覆燾之恩著矣，而瘡痍未復；

translations.literal: The favor of sheltering warmth is evident, yet the wounds are not yet healed;
translations.idiomatic: The sheltering grace of Your Majesty is already clear, yet the wounds of the realm are not yet healed;

sentences.zh: 德教之風被矣，而資產屢空。

translations.literal: The wind of virtue and instruction has spread, yet assets are repeatedly emptied.
translations.idiomatic: the wind of virtue and instruction has spread, yet people's means are repeatedly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 是以古人譬之種樹，年祀綿遠，則枝葉扶疏；

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients compared this to planting trees: when years and sacrifices extend far, then branches and leaves spread luxuriantly;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients compared this to planting a tree: when years stretch on, its branches and leaves grow thick;

sentences.zh: 若種之日淺，根本未固，雖壅之以黑墳，暖之以春日，一人搖之，必致枯槁。

translations.literal: if the day of planting is shallow and the root and base are not yet firm, though heaped with dark soil and warmed by spring sun, one man's shake will surely bring withering and desiccation.
translations.idiomatic: but if it has been planted only recently and its roots are not yet firm, then though it is heaped with rich soil and warmed by spring sun, one man's shake will make it wither and die.

sentences.zh: 今之百姓，頗類於此。

translations.literal: Today's common people greatly resemble this.
translations.idiomatic: The common people of today greatly resemble this.

sentences.zh: 常加含養，則日就滋息；

translations.literal: Constantly given nurturing care, day by day they approach increase and flourishing;
translations.idiomatic: If constantly nurtured, they will day by day grow and flourish;

sentences.zh: 暫有征役，則隨而凋耗。

translations.literal: briefly subjected to levies and corvée, they accordingly wither and deplete.
translations.idiomatic: but if levies and corvée are imposed even briefly, they at once decline and waste away.

sentences.zh: 凋耗既甚，則人不卿生；

translations.literal: When withering and depletion are extreme, then people cannot make a living;
translations.idiomatic: When depletion becomes extreme, people cannot make a living;

sentences.zh: 人不卿生，則怨氣充塞；

translations.literal: When people cannot make a living, then resentful qi fills and blocks all;
translations.idiomatic: when people cannot make a living, resentment fills the land;

sentences.zh: 怨氣充塞，則離叛之心生矣。

translations.literal: When resentful qi fills and blocks all, then hearts of separation and rebellion arise.
translations.idiomatic: when resentment fills the land, hearts turn toward separation and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 故帝舜曰：「可愛非君，可畏非人。」

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Shun said: "What is to be cherished is not the ruler; what is to be feared is not other men."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Emperor Shun said, "What is to be cherished is not the ruler alone; what is to be feared is not other men."

sentences.zh: 孔安國曰：「人以君爲命，故可愛；

translations.literal: Kong Anguo said: "People take the ruler as their mandate, therefore he is cherishable;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo said, "The people take the ruler as their livelihood, and therefore he may be cherished;

sentences.zh: 君失道，人叛之，故可畏。」

translations.literal: When the ruler loses the Way and people rebel against him, therefore he is to be feared."
translations.idiomatic: but when the ruler loses the Way and the people rebel, he becomes something to be feared."

sentences.zh: 仲尼曰：「君猶舟也，人猶水也；

translations.literal: Zhongni said: "The ruler is like a boat, and the people are like water;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "The ruler is like a boat and the people like water;

sentences.zh: 水所以載舟，亦所以覆舟。」

translations.literal: water is that by which the boat is carried, and also that by which the boat is overturned."
translations.idiomatic: water carries the boat, and water also overturns the boat."

sentences.zh: 是以古之哲王，雖休勿休，日慎一日者，良爲此也。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage kings of antiquity, though at rest did not rest, and were daily cautious over daily—truly for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the sage kings of antiquity, though at rest would not rest, and grew more cautious day by day.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下覽古今之事，察安危之機，上以社稷爲重，下以億兆爲念。

translations.literal: Humbly I pray Your Majesty will survey affairs ancient and modern, discern the mechanism of safety and peril, above take the altars of state as weighty, and below take the myriad multitudes to heart.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will review events past and present, discern the turning points of safety and danger, hold the altars of state above all else, and keep the myriad people in mind.

sentences.zh: 明選舉，慎賞罰，進賢才，退不肖。

translations.literal: Clearly select and appoint, carefully bestow rewards and punishments, advance worthy talent, and retire the unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Choose officials wisely, reward and punish with care, advance the worthy, and dismiss the unfit.

sentences.zh: 聞過即改，從諫如流。

translations.literal: Hearing faults, immediately reform; receiving remonstrance like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Correct faults as soon as you hear them, and accept remonstrance as freely as flowing water.

sentences.zh: 爲善在於不疑，出令期於必信。

translations.literal: Doing good lies in not doubting; issuing orders expects certainty of faith.
translations.idiomatic: Do good without hesitation, and issue orders only when they can be trusted to the end.

sentences.zh: 頤神養性，省畋游之娛；

translations.literal: Nourish spirit and cultivate nature, and reduce the pleasures of hunting outings;
translations.idiomatic: Nourish your spirit and temper your nature, and reduce the pleasures of hunting and travel;

sentences.zh: 去奢從儉，減工役之費。

translations.literal: Discard extravagance and follow frugality, and reduce the expenses of labor and service.
translations.idiomatic: cast off extravagance and follow frugality, and cut the costs of labor and public works.

sentences.zh: 務靜方內而不求闢土；

translations.literal: Devote effort to tranquility within the realm and do not seek to open new lands;
translations.idiomatic: Devote yourself to peace within the realm and do not seek to expand territory or open new lands;

sentences.zh: 載橐弓矢而無忘武備。

translations.literal: Carry bow and arrows in the quiver and do not forget martial preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: keep bow and arrows in the quiver, yet never forget military preparedness.

sentences.zh: 凡此數者，雖爲國之常道，陛下之所常行，臣之愚心，唯願陛下思之而不倦，行之而不怠。

translations.literal: All these several points, though they are the constant Way of governing the state and what Your Majesty constantly practices, in my foolish heart I only wish Your Majesty would think on them without wearying and practice them without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: All these points, though they are the constant principles of governing a state and things Your Majesty already often practices, are what my humble heart wishes Your Majesty would ponder without weariness and carry out without slackening.

sentences.zh: 則至道之美，與三、五比隆；

translations.literal: Then the beauty of the supreme Way would rise alongside the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors;
translations.idiomatic: Then the splendor of the supreme Way would stand equal to that of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors;

sentences.zh: 億載之祚，隨天地長久。

translations.literal: The throne of ten thousand years would endure as long as heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: and Your throne would endure as long as heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 雖使桑谷爲妖，龍蛇作孽，雉雊於鼎耳，石言於晉地，猶當轉禍爲福，變咎爲祥。

translations.literal: Even if mulberry and grain became portents, dragons and serpents wrought calamity, pheasants crowed at cauldron ears, and stones spoke in Jin lands, one should still turn disaster into blessing and transform ill omen into auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Even if mulberry and grain became omens, dragons and serpents wrought havoc, pheasants crowed from cauldron handles, and stones spoke in the land of Jin, you would still turn disaster into blessing and ill omen into good fortune.

sentences.zh: 況水雨之患，陰陽常理，豈可謂之天譴而系聖心哉？

translations.literal: How much more is flooding from rain a matter of yin and yang's usual principle—how can it be called heaven's reprimand and tied to the sagely heart?
translations.idiomatic: How much less should flooding and rain—ordinary workings of yin and yang—be called a heavenly reprimand and allowed to weigh upon Your Majesty's mind?

sentences.zh: 臣聞古人有言：「農夫勞而君子養焉，愚者言而智者擇焉。」

translations.literal: Your subject has heard the ancients say: "The farmer toils and the gentleman is nourished thereby; the foolish speak and the wise choose therefrom."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard the ancients say, "The farmer toils and the gentleman is nourished by his labor; the foolish speak and the wise choose among their words."

sentences.zh: 輒陳狂瞽，伏待斧鉞。

translations.literal: Rashly I present wild and blind words; humbly I await the axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: I have rashly offered these ignorant words and humbly await Your Majesty's judgment.

sentences.zh: 是時魏王泰寵冠諸王，盛修第宅，文本以爲侈不可長，上疏盛陳節儉之義，言泰宜有抑損，太宗並嘉之，賜帛三百段。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Wei, Li Tai, in favor crowned all princes and lavishly built mansions. Wenben thought extravagance must not be indulged, memorialized fully stating the meaning of frugality, and said Tai ought to have restraint and reduction. Taizong praised both and bestowed three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Wei, Li Tai, was favored above all the princes and built mansions on a grand scale. Wenben believed extravagance must not be allowed to grow, and memorialized at length on the virtue of frugality, urging that Tai's expenditures be curbed. Taizong approved of both points and bestowed three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 十七年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Blue Light.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Blue Light.

sentences.zh: 文本自以出自書生，每懷捴損。

translations.literal: Wenben himself, because he came from a scholar background, always harbored self-restraint and modesty.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben, considering himself no more than a scholar by origin, always practiced self-restraint and modesty.

sentences.zh: 平生故人，雖微賤必與之抗禮。

translations.literal: Old friends of his whole life, though humble and lowly, he always treated with equal courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Toward old friends from his earlier life, however humble their station, he always treated them as equals.

sentences.zh: 居處卑陋，室無茵褥帷帳之飾。

translations.literal: His dwelling was humble and shabby; the rooms had no mats, cushions, curtains, or hangings for ornament.
translations.idiomatic: His home was plain and modest, and his rooms had none of the usual mats, cushions, curtains, or hangings.

sentences.zh: 事母以孝聞，撫弟侄恩義甚篤。

translations.literal: He was known for filial service to his mother, and in raising his younger brother and nephews his kindness and righteousness were very deep.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for filial devotion to his mother, and in caring for his younger brother and nephews he showed deep kindness and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 太宗每言其「弘厚忠謹，吾親之信之。」

translations.literal: Taizong often said of him: "Magnanimous, thick, loyal, and careful—I personally am close to him and trust him."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong often said of him, "He is broad-minded, steadfast, loyal, and careful. I am close to him and trust him."

sentences.zh: 是時，新立晉王爲皇太子，名士多兼領宮官，太宗欲令文本兼攝。

translations.literal: At that time the newly established Prince of Jin as crown prince—many famous scholars concurrently held palace offices, and Taizong wished Wenben to hold concurrent charge.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Jin had just been made crown prince. Many eminent men also held posts in the Eastern Palace, and Taizong wished Wenben to serve in such a concurrent capacity.

sentences.zh: 文本再拜曰：「臣以庸才，久逾涯分，守此一職，猶懼滿盈，豈宜更忝春坊，以速時謗。

translations.literal: Wenben bowed twice and said: "Your subject with mediocre talent has long exceeded my proper measure. Guarding this one post, I still fear filling to overflow—how should I further disgrace the Spring Palace and hasten timely slander?
translations.idiomatic: Wenben bowed twice and said, "Your servant is a man of mediocre talent who has long exceeded his proper station. Even in holding this one office I still fear overreaching myself. How could I further disgrace the Eastern Palace and invite timely slander?

sentences.zh: 臣請一心以事陛下，不願更希東宮恩澤。」

translations.literal: Your subject requests to serve Your Majesty with a single heart and does not wish further to seek grace from the Eastern Palace."
translations.idiomatic: I ask only to serve Your Majesty with undivided loyalty and do not wish to seek further favor from the Eastern Palace."

sentences.zh: 太宗乃止。

translations.literal: Taizong thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong thereupon desisted.

sentences.zh: 仍令五日一參東宮，皇太子執賓友之禮，與之答拜。

translations.literal: Still he ordered Wenben to attend the Eastern Palace once every five days; the crown prince performed guest-and-friend ritual and exchanged bows with him.
translations.idiomatic: He still ordered Wenben to attend the Eastern Palace once every five days, and the crown prince treated him with the courtesy due a guest and friend, exchanging bows with him in reply.

sentences.zh: 其見待如此。

translations.literal: The honor shown him was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the honor shown him.

sentences.zh: 俄拜中書令，歸家有憂色，其母怪而問之，文本曰：「非勳非舊，濫荷寵榮，責重位高，所以憂懼。」

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Director of the Secretariat. Returning home with a troubled expression, his mother wondered and asked him. Wenben said: "Neither merit nor old association—I have loosely borne favor and glory; heavy responsibility and high position are why I worry and fear."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Director of the Secretariat. He returned home with a troubled look, and his mother, surprised, asked why. Wenben said, "I have neither merit nor long association with the throne, yet I have undeservedly received favor and glory. My responsibilities are heavy and my rank is high—that is why I am anxious and afraid."

sentences.zh: 親賓有來慶賀，輒曰：「今受吊，不受賀也。」

translations.literal: Relatives and guests who came to congratulate, he would say: "Today I accept condolences, not congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: When relatives and guests came to congratulate him, he would say, "Today I accept condolences, not congratulations."

sentences.zh: 又有勸其營產業者，文本嘆曰：「南方一布衣，徒歩入關，疇昔之望，不過秘書郎、一縣令耳。

translations.literal: There were also those who urged him to manage property. Wenben sighed and said: "A plain-clothed man of the south, entering the pass on foot—in former days my hope was no more than Secretariat Secretary and a county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to build up an estate. Wenben sighed and said, "I was once a plain-clothed man from the south who entered the pass on foot. In those days my highest hope was no more than to become a Secretariat Secretary or a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 而無汗馬之勞，徒以文墨致位中書令，斯亦極矣。

translations.literal: Yet without sweat-of-horse toil, by literary ink alone reaching Director of the Secretariat—this also is the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet without any toil of horse and sword, I have reached the post of Director of the Secretariat through writing alone. That is already the utmost.

sentences.zh: 荷俸祿之重，爲懼已多，何得更言產業乎？」

translations.literal: Bearing the weight of salary and emoluments, my fears are already many—how could I further speak of property?"
translations.idiomatic: I already have more than enough reason to fear while bearing such heavy salary and emoluments. How could I speak further of building an estate?"

sentences.zh: 言者嘆息而退。

translations.literal: The speaker sighed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The man sighed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 文本既久在樞揆，當涂任事，賞錫稠疊，凡有財物出入，皆委季弟文昭，一無所問。

translations.literal: Wenben, having long been in the pivot and council, held power on the road and received rewards and gifts dense and layered. For all property going in and out he entrusted everything to his youngest brother Wenzhao, never questioning anything.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben had long served at the center of government and wielded real power. Rewards and gifts came to him in great profusion, yet for all property entering or leaving his household he entrusted everything to his youngest brother Wenzhao and never questioned any of it.

sentences.zh: 文昭時任校書郎，多與時人遊款，太宗聞而不悅，嘗從容謂文本曰：「卿弟過多交結，恐累卿，朕將出之爲外官，如何？」

translations.literal: Wenzhao then served as Collator and associated much with men of the time. Taizong heard this and was displeased. Once, genially, he told Wenben: "Your younger brother has too much socializing—I fear it may burden you. I wish to send him out as an outer official—what say you?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao was then serving as Collator and kept company with many men of the day. Taizong heard of this and was displeased. Once he spoke gently to Wenben, saying, "Your younger brother keeps too many acquaintances, and I fear it may harm you. I intend to send him out as a local official. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 文本泣曰：「臣弟少孤，老母特所鍾念，不欲信宿離於左右。

translations.literal: Wenben wept and said: "Your subject's younger brother was orphaned young. Our old mother especially dotes on him and does not wish even one night's lodging separated from her side.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben wept and said, "My younger brother lost his father while still young, and our old mother dotes on him above all. She cannot bear even one night without him at her side.

sentences.zh: 若今外出，母必憂悴，儻無此弟，亦無老母也。」

translations.literal: If sent out now, mother would surely grieve and waste away; if without this younger brother, there would also be no old mother."
translations.idiomatic: If he were sent away now, my mother would surely grieve herself to death. Without this younger brother, I would have no old mother left."

sentences.zh: 歔欷嗚咽，太宗愍其意而止。

translations.literal: Sobbing and choking with tears, Taizong sympathized with his meaning and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He sobbed and wept until he could hardly speak. Taizong was moved by his plea and desisted.

sentences.zh: 唯召見文昭，嚴加誡約，亦卒無愆過。

translations.literal: Only Wenzhao was summoned and seen; he was strictly admonished and bound, and in the end there were no faults.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned Wenzhao alone and sternly warned him, and in the end Wenzhao committed no further fault.

sentences.zh: 及將伐遼，凡所籌度，一皆委之。

translations.literal: When about to campaign against Liao, all planning was wholly entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor prepared to campaign against Liaodong, all planning was wholly entrusted to Wenben.

sentences.zh: 文本受委既深，神情頓竭，言辭舉措，頗異平常。

translations.literal: Wenben, having received deep trust, suddenly exhausted his spirit and expression; his words and deportment greatly differed from the usual.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben, burdened with this deep trust, was suddenly drained in body and spirit, and his speech and bearing were quite unlike his usual self.

sentences.zh: 太宗見而憂之，謂左右曰：「文本今與我同行，恐不與我同返。」

translations.literal: Taizong saw this and was worried. He told those at his side: "Wenben today goes with me—I fear he will not return with me."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong saw this and was troubled. He told those around him, "Wenben is going with me now, but I fear he will not return with me."

sentences.zh: 及至幽州，遇暴疾，太宗親自臨視，撫之流涕。

translations.literal: When they reached Youzhou, he encountered sudden illness. Taizong personally came to visit bedside and, stroking him, shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Youzhou, Wenben fell suddenly ill. Taizong visited him in person, stroked him, and wept.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: Soon he died, age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 其夕，太宗聞嚴鼓之聲，曰：「文本殞逝，情深惻怛。

translations.literal: That evening Taizong heard the sound of the strict drum and said: "Wenben has fallen and passed—deep is my sorrow and tenderness.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Taizong heard the midnight watch drum and said, "Wenben has died, and my grief is deep.

sentences.zh: 今宵夜警，所不忍聞。」

translations.literal: Tonight's midnight alarm—I cannot bear to hear it."
translations.idiomatic: Tonight's midnight alarm is something I cannot bear to hear."

sentences.zh: 命停之。

translations.literal: He ordered it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it stopped.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、廣州都督，謚曰憲，賜東園秘器，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Area Commander of Guangzhou; posthumous title Xian; bestowed Eastern Garden secret coffin; buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Palace Attendant and Area Commander of Guangzhou, given the posthumous name Xian, granted the Eastern Garden secret coffin, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 有集六十捲行於代。

translations.literal: He had a collected works of sixty scrolls circulating in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works, sixty scrolls in all, circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 文本兄子 長倩文本兄文叔。

translations.literal: Wenben's elder brother's son Changqian; Wenben's elder brother Wenshu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben's elder brother's son Changqian and Wenben's elder brother Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 文叔子長倩，少爲文本所鞠，同於己子。

translations.literal: Wenshu's son Changqian, in youth was nurtured by Wenben, the same as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu's son Changqian was raised from boyhood by Wenben as though he were Wenben's own child.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，累轉兵部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the Yongchun era, he was repeatedly transferred to Vice Minister of War and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchun reign he rose through successive appointments to Vice Minister of War and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，自夏官尚書遷內史，知夏官事，俄拜文昌右相，封鄧國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chuigong, he moved from Minister of the Department of Summer Affairs to Interior Secretary, overseeing Summer Affairs, and soon was appointed Right Chancellor of Wenchang and enfeoffed as Duke of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chuigong era he was promoted from Minister of the Department of Summer Affairs to Interior Secretary while retaining charge of that department; before long he was made Right Chancellor of Wenchang and enfeoffed as Duke of Deng.

sentences.zh: 則天初革命，尤好符瑞，長倩懼罪，頗有陳奏，又上疏請改皇嗣姓爲武氏，以爲周室儲貳，則天許之，實封五百戸。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu first changed the dynasty, she especially favored portents and omens. Changqian feared guilt and made several memorials; he also submitted a memorial asking that the imperial heir's surname be changed to Wu so that he might serve as heir of the Zhou house. Empress Wu approved this and granted him an actual fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zetian first seized power and remade the dynasty, she was especially fond of auspicious omens. Fearful of falling under suspicion, Changqian submitted several memorials and even petitioned that the crown prince's surname be changed to Wu so he could stand as heir of the new Zhou dynasty. Wu Zetian consented and granted him a substantive fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 天授二年，加特進、輔國大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshou, he was additionally granted the rank of Tejin and the title Grand General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshou he received the additional honors of Tejin rank and Grand General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 其年，鳳閣舍人張嘉福與洛州人王慶之等列名上表，請立武承嗣爲皇太子。

translations.literal: That year, Phoenix Pavilion Attendant Zhang Jiafu and Wang Qingzhi of Luozhou and others submitted a memorial with their names listed, requesting that Wu Chengsi be established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Zhang Jiafu, an attender of the Phoenix Pavilion, and Wang Qingzhi of Luozhou, together with others, submitted a joint memorial asking that Wu Chengsi be made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 長倩以皇嗣在東宮，不可更立承嗣，與地官尚書格輔元竟不署名，仍奏請切責上書者。

translations.literal: Changqian argued that since the imperial heir was already in the Eastern Palace, Chengsi could not be established in his place. He and Minister of the Department of Earth Affairs Ge Fuyuan ultimately refused to sign, and still memorialized requesting stern punishment of those who had submitted the petition.
translations.idiomatic: Changqian held that with an imperial heir already installed in the Eastern Palace, Chengsi could not be elevated in his stead. He and Ge Fuyuan, Minister of the Department of Earth Affairs, refused to sign the memorial altogether and submitted a separate petition demanding severe punishment for the petitioners.

sentences.zh: 由是大忤諸武意，乃斥令西征吐蕃，充武威道行軍大總管。

translations.literal: Because of this he greatly offended the Wu clan's wishes and was sent away on a western campaign against Tibet, serving as Grand Commander of the Wuwei Circuit army.
translations.idiomatic: This deeply affronted the Wu clan, and he was dispatched on a western expedition against Tibet as Grand Commander of the Wuwei Circuit army.

sentences.zh: 中路召還，下制獄，被誅，仍發掘其父祖墳墓。

translations.literal: Midway he was recalled, thrown into the secret prison, executed, and the tombs of his father and grandfather were excavated.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled before reaching his destination, thrown into the secret prison, and executed; the graves of his father and grandfather were then dug up as well.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣又脅迫長倩子靈源，令誣納言歐陽通及格輔元等數十人，皆陷以同反之罪，並誅死。

translations.literal: Lai Junchen also coerced Changqian's son Lingyuan to falsely accuse Grand Counselor Ouyang Tong, Ge Fuyuan, and several dozen others, all of whom were framed on charges of treason and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen then coerced Changqian's son Lingyuan into falsely implicating Grand Counselor Ouyang Tong, Ge Fuyuan, and dozens of others in a conspiracy; all were condemned for treason and put to death.

sentences.zh: 長倩子 羲長倩子羲，長安中爲廣武令，有能名。

translations.literal: Changqian's son Xi. Xi, during the Chang'an era, served as Magistrate of Guangwu and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Changqian's son Xi served as magistrate of Guangwu during the Chang'an era and was known for his competence.

sentences.zh: 則天嘗令宰相各舉堪爲員外郎者，鳳閣侍郎韋嗣立薦羲，且奏曰：「恨其從父長倩犯逆爲累。」

translations.literal: Empress Wu once ordered each chancellor to recommend someone suitable to serve as a vice director. Phoenix Pavilion Vice Director Wei Sili recommended Xi and memorialized, saying, "It is regrettable that his paternal uncle Changqian's crime of rebellion is a burden upon him."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian once instructed each chancellor to nominate someone fit for appointment as a vice director. Wei Sili, Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion, recommended Xi but added in his memorial, "It is a pity that his paternal uncle Changqian's conviction for treason weighs against him."

sentences.zh: 則天曰：「苟有材幹，何恨微累？」

translations.literal: Empress Wu said, "If he possesses talent and ability, why regret a minor burden?"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian replied, "If he has talent and ability, what does a slight stain matter?"

sentences.zh: 遂拜天官員外郎。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Vice Director of the Department of Heavenly Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was promptly appointed Vice Director of the Department of Heavenly Affairs.

sentences.zh: 由是緣坐近親，相次入省，登封令劉守悌爲司門員外郎，渭南令裴惓爲地官員外郎。

translations.literal: Because of this, close relatives implicated by association entered the ministries in succession: Dengfeng Magistrate Liu Shouti became Vice Director of the Gate Department, and Weinan Magistrate Pei Juan became Vice Director of the Earth Department.
translations.idiomatic: Through this connection, close kinsmen were drawn into office one after another: Liu Shouti, magistrate of Dengfeng, became Vice Director of the Gate Department, and Pei Juan, magistrate of Weinan, became Vice Director of the Earth Department.

sentences.zh: 先是，羲爲金壇令，守悌及惓稱爲清德。

translations.literal: Previously Xi had been Magistrate of Jintan, while Shouti and Juan were praised for pure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xi had served as magistrate of Jintan, while Shouti and Juan were already known for their upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 羲以文吏著名，俱爲巡察使所薦，皆授畿縣令，又同爲尚書郎，悉有美譽。

translations.literal: Xi was famous as a civil official. All were recommended by circuit inspectors, all were granted magistracies in the capital region, and again served together as directors in the ministries, each enjoying a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was renowned as a capable civil administrator. All three had been recommended by touring inspectors and appointed magistrates in the capital districts; when they later served together as ministry directors, each enjoyed an excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 守悌後至陝州刺史，惓至杭州刺史。

translations.literal: Shouti later rose to Prefect of Shaanzhou, and Juan to Prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shouti later became prefect of Shaanzhou, and Juan became prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 羲，神龍初爲中書舍人。

translations.literal: Xi, at the beginning of Shenlong, served as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shenlong era, Xi served as a drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時武三思用事，侍中敬暉欲上表請削諸武之爲王者，募爲疏者。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Sansi held power. Palace Attendant Jing Hui wished to submit a memorial requesting that all members of the Wu clan who had been made kings be stripped of their titles, and sought someone to draft the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Sansi dominated the court. Palace Attendant Jing Hui wanted to submit a memorial calling for the Wu princes to be stripped of their royal titles and sought someone to draft it.

sentences.zh: 眾畏三思，皆辭托不敢爲之，羲便操筆，辭甚切直。

translations.literal: All feared Sansi and declined on various pretexts, not daring to do it. Xi immediately took up the brush, and his language was very sharp and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone feared Sansi and found excuses to refuse, but Xi took up the brush at once and wrote in language that was blunt and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 由是忤三思意，轉秘書少監，再遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Because of this he offended Sansi's wishes, was transferred to Deputy Director of the Secretariat Archive, and was later promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: This offended Sansi, and Xi was transferred to Deputy Director of the Secretariat Archive before being promoted again to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時吏部侍郎崔湜、太常少卿鄭愔、大理少卿李元恭分掌選事，皆以贓貨聞，羲最守正，時議美之。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Minister of Personnel Cui Xian, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zheng Yin, and Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Li Yuangong divided responsibility for selection affairs; all were known for bribery, while Xi was the most upright, and contemporary opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cui Xian, Vice Minister of Personnel, Zheng Yin, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Li Yuangong, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, shared control over official appointments, and all were notorious for taking bribes. Xi alone held the line, and public opinion commended him.

sentences.zh: 尋加銀青光祿大夫、右散騎常侍、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally granted Silver Blue Light Grand Master of the Imperial Household, Right Regular Attendant, and Third Rank Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was further honored with the ranks of Silver Blue Light Grand Master and Right Regular Attendant, and with appointment as Third Rank Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，出爲陝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Xi was sent out as Prefect of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong ascended the throne, Xi was posted out as prefect of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 復歷刑部、戸部二尚書，門下三品，監修國史，刪定格令，仍修《氏族錄》。

translations.literal: He again served as Minister of the Ministries of Justice and Revenue, held Third Rank at the Chancellery, supervised compilation of the National History, edited statutes and regulations, and also compiled the Records of Clans.
translations.idiomatic: He later served again as Minister of Justice and Minister of Revenue, held Third Rank at the Chancellery, supervised the National History, revised statutes and administrative codes, and also compiled the Records of Clans.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗時，侍御史冉祖雍誣奏睿宗及太平公主與節愍太子連謀，請加推究，羲與中書侍郎蕭至忠密申保護。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the reign of Emperor Zhongzong, Attending Censor Ran Zuyong falsely memorialized that Emperor Ruizong and Princess Taiping had conspired with Crown Prince Jiemin and requested a thorough investigation. Xi and Secretariat Vice Director Xiao Zhizhong secretly pleaded on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Zhongzong's reign, Attending Censor Ran Zuyong falsely accused Ruizong and Princess Taiping of plotting with Crown Prince Jiemin and called for a full investigation. Xi and Xiao Zhizhong, Vice Director of the Secretariat, secretly intervened on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 及羲監修《中宗實錄》，自書其事，睿宗覽而大加賞嘆，賜物三百段、良馬一匹，仍下制書褒美之。

translations.literal: When Xi supervised compilation of the Veritable Record of Emperor Zhongzong and wrote this affair himself, Ruizong read it and greatly praised and sighed over it, bestowing three hundred bolts of goods and one fine horse, and still issued an edict commending him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi, as supervisor of the Veritable Record of Emperor Zhongzong, recorded the episode in his own hand, Ruizong read the account and was deeply moved; he rewarded Xi with three hundred bolts of silk and a fine horse and issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 時羲兄獻爲國子司業，弟翔爲陝州刺史，休爲商州刺史，從族兄弟子侄，因羲引用登清要者數十人。

translations.literal: At the time Xi's elder brother Xian was Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, his younger brother Xiang was Prefect of Shaanzhou, and Xiu was Prefect of Shangzhou; collateral brothers, sons, and nephews—through Xi's recommendations, several dozen reached important posts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xi's elder brother Xian served as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, his brother Xiang was prefect of Shaanzhou, and his brother Xiu was prefect of Shangzhou; through Xi's patronage, dozens of cousins, nephews, and other kinsmen were placed in prestigious offices.

sentences.zh: 羲嘆曰：「物極則返，可以懼矣！」

translations.literal: Xi sighed and said, "When things reach their extreme they turn back—this should inspire fear!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi sighed and said, "When things reach their limit they reverse—this ought to give one pause!"

sentences.zh: 然竟不能有所抑退。

translations.literal: Yet in the end he could not restrain or dismiss any of them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he could not bring himself to restrain or turn any of them away.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 先天元年，坐預太平公主謀逆伏誅，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantian, for participating in Princess Taiping's plot of rebellion he was executed, and his household property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiantian he was executed for taking part in Princess Taiping's conspiracy, and his family's property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 附 格輔元格輔元者，汴州浚儀人也。

translations.literal: Appendix: Ge Fuyuan. Ge Fuyuan was a native of Junyi in Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Ge Fuyuan. Ge Fuyuan was a native of Junyi in Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 伯父德仁，隋剡縣丞，與同郡人齊王文學王孝逸、文林郎繁師玄、羅川郡戸曹靖君亮、司隸從事鄭祖咸、宣城縣長鄭師善、王世充中書舍人李行簡、處士盧協等八人，以辭學擅名，當時號爲「陳留八俊」。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Deren was Assistant Magistrate of Yan County in the Sui dynasty. Together with eight men of the same commandery—Literary Companion to the Prince of Qi Wang Xiaoyi, Gentleman of the Forest of Letters Fan Shixuan, Registrar of Households of Luochuan Commandery Jing Junliang, Clerk of the Directorate of Justice Zheng Zuxian, District Magistrate of Xuancheng Zheng Shishan, Secretariat Drafter under Wang Shichong Li Xingjian, and Recluse Lu Xie—they were famed for literary learning and were called at the time the "Eight Worthies of Chenliu."
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Deren had been assistant magistrate of Yan County under the Sui. He and seven others from the same region—Wang Xiaoyi, literary companion to the Prince of Qi; Fan Shixuan, Gentleman of the Forest of Letters; Jing Junliang, registrar of Luochuan Commandery; Zheng Zuxian, clerk of the Directorate of Justice; Zheng Shishan, magistrate of Xuancheng District; Li Xingjian, a secretariat drafter under Wang Shichong; and the recluse Lu Xie—were celebrated for their literary talent and were known in their day as the "Eight Worthies of Chenliu."

sentences.zh: 輔元弱冠舉明經，歷遷御史大夫、地官尚書、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: Fuyuan, at the age of twenty, passed the Mingjing examination and was successively promoted to Censor-in-Chief, Minister of the Department of Earth Affairs, and Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyuan passed the Mingjing examination in his early twenties and rose through the ranks to Censor-in-Chief, Minister of the Department of Earth Affairs, and Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 初，張嘉福等請立武承嗣也，則天以問輔元，固稱不可，遂爲承嗣所譖而死，海內冤之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jiafu and others had requested that Wu Chengsi be established as heir, Empress Wu asked Fuyuan's view; he firmly declared it impossible. He was then slandered by Chengsi and put to death, and the realm considered it a grievous injustice.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jiafu and the others petitioned to make Wu Chengsi crown prince, Wu Zetian asked Fuyuan's opinion; he firmly declared the proposal unacceptable. Chengsi then slandered him, and he was executed—a verdict widely regarded throughout the empire as a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 輔元兄希元，高宗時洛州司法參軍，章懷太子召令與洗馬劉訥言等註解范曄《後漢書》，行於代。

translations.literal: Fuyuan's elder brother Xiyuan, during the reign of Emperor Gaozong, was Legal Assistant of Luozhou. Crown Prince Zhanghuai summoned him, together with Palace Steward Liu Neyan and others, to annotate Fan Ye's Book of the Later Han, which circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyuan's elder brother Xiyuan served as legal assistant in Luozhou under Emperor Gaozong. Crown Prince Zhanghuai summoned him, together with the palace steward Liu Neyan and others, to produce a commentary on Fan Ye's Book of the Later Han, which circulated widely in their time.

sentences.zh: 先輔元卒。

translations.literal: He died before Fuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died before his brother Fuyuan.

sentences.zh: 杜正倫杜正倫，相州洹水人也。

translations.literal: Du Zhenglun was a native of Huanshui in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhenglun was a native of Huanshui in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽中，與兄正玄、正藏俱以秀才擢第。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era of the Sui, he and his elder brothers Zhengxuan and Zhengcang all passed the Xiucai examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era of the Sui dynasty, he and his elder brothers Zhengxuan and Zhengcang all passed the Xiucai examination.

sentences.zh: 隋代舉秀才止十餘人，正倫一家有三秀才，甚爲當時稱美。

translations.literal: In the Sui dynasty only a little more than ten men were selected as Xiucai; Zhenglun's household had three Xiucai and was greatly praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, fewer than a dozen candidates ever passed the Xiucai examination in a given year; that three brothers from Zhenglun's family did so was widely admired in their day.

sentences.zh: 正倫善屬文，深明釋典。

translations.literal: Zhenglun was skilled at literary composition and deeply versed in Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun was an accomplished writer and deeply versed in Buddhist scripture.

sentences.zh: 仕隋爲羽騎尉。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as Captain of Feathered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as Captain of Feathered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 武德中，歷遷齊州總管府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: During Wude, he was successively promoted to Recording Secretary in the headquarters of the Area Command of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude era he rose to the post of recording secretary in the headquarters of the Qizhou area command.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞其名，令直秦府文學館。

translations.literal: Taizong heard his name and ordered him to serve directly in the Literary Institute of the Prince of Qin's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of him, he had Zhenglun assigned to the Literary Institute of the Prince of Qin's mansion.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，尚書右丞魏徵表薦正倫，以爲古今難匹，遂擢授兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Wei Zheng memorialized recommending Zhenglun, declaring him unmatched in past and present, and he was thereupon promoted and appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan, Wei Zheng, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, recommended Zhenglun in a memorial as a man without equal in any age, and Zhenglun was promptly appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂曰：「朕今令舉行能之人，非朕獨私於行能者，以其能益於百姓也。

translations.literal: Taizong said to him, "I now order the promotion of men of conduct and ability—not because I favor such men for my own sake alone, but because their ability benefits the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told him, "I am promoting men of talent and integrity now—not because I favor such men for personal reasons, but because their abilities serve the people.

sentences.zh: 朕於宗親及以勳舊無行能者，終不任之。

translations.literal: As for my kinsmen by blood and my old meritorious followers who lack conduct and ability, I will never appoint them.
translations.idiomatic: Even among my own kin and old comrades-in-arms, I will never appoint anyone who lacks talent and integrity.

sentences.zh: 以卿忠直，朕今舉卿，卿宜勉稱所舉。」

translations.literal: Because you are loyal and upright, I now promote you; you should strive to live up to what has been expected in promoting you."
translations.idiomatic: Because you are loyal and upright, I am promoting you now; strive to prove worthy of the trust I am placing in you."

sentences.zh: 二年，拜給事中，兼知起居注。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Supervising Secretary and concurrently placed in charge of the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Supervising Secretary and given charge of the Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗謂侍臣曰：「朕每日坐朝，欲出一言，即思此言於百姓有利益否，所以不能多言。」

translations.literal: Taizong once said to his attending ministers, "Each day when I hold court, whenever I wish to speak a word, I immediately consider whether this word will benefit the common people; therefore I cannot speak much."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once told his ministers, "Every day when I hold court, before I utter a single word I ask myself whether it will benefit the people—which is why I speak so little."

sentences.zh: 正倫進曰：「君舉必書，言存左右史。

translations.literal: Zhenglun stepped forward and said, "The ruler's actions must be recorded, and his words are preserved by the left and right historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun stepped forward and said, "A ruler's every act is recorded, and his words are preserved by the court historiographers.

sentences.zh: 臣職當修起居注，不敢不盡愚直。

translations.literal: My duty is to compile the Daily Records, and I dare not fail to offer all my blunt sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: It is my duty to maintain the Daily Records, and I dare not withhold my honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 陛下若一言乖於道理，則千載累於聖德，非直當今損於百姓，願陛下慎之。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty speaks one word contrary to reason, it will burden your sagely virtue for a thousand generations—not merely harm the common people in the present day. I beg Your Majesty to be cautious."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty speaks even one word at odds with principle, it will stain your reputation for a thousand years—not merely harm the people of today. I beg Your Majesty to weigh your words carefully."

sentences.zh: 太宗大悅，賜絹二百段。

translations.literal: Taizong was greatly pleased and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was greatly pleased and rewarded him with two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 四年，累遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was successively promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 六年，正倫與御史大夫韋挺、秘書少監虞世南、著作郎姚思廉等咸上封事稱旨，太宗爲之設宴，因謂曰：「朕歷觀自古人臣立忠之事，若值明王，便得盡誠規諫，至如龍逢、比干，竟不免孥戮。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Zhenglun, together with Censor-in-Chief Wei Ting, Deputy Director of the Secretariat Archive Yu Shinan, Director of Compilation Yao Silian, and others, all submitted sealed memorials that pleased the emperor. Taizong held a banquet for them and therefore said, "I have reviewed throughout history how ministers established loyalty: if they encountered an enlightened ruler, they could fully offer sincere remonstrance; yet men such as Long Feng and Bi Gan still could not escape execution extending to their families.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhenglun, together with Censor-in-Chief Wei Ting, Deputy Director of the Secretariat Archive Yu Shinan, Director of Compilation Yao Silian, and others, submitted sealed memorials that pleased the emperor. Taizong held a banquet in their honor and said, "Looking back through history at ministers who gave loyal counsel, those who served enlightened rulers could speak freely—yet even Long Feng and Bi Gan could not escape death, and their families perished with them.

sentences.zh: 爲君不易，爲臣極難。

translations.literal: To be a ruler is not easy; to be a minister is extremely difficult.
translations.idiomatic: To be a ruler is no easy thing; to be a loyal minister is harder still.

sentences.zh: 我又聞龍可擾而馴，然喉下有逆鱗，觸之則殺人。

translations.literal: I have also heard that a dragon can be tamed and made docile, yet beneath its throat there are inverted scales; touch them and it kills a man.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that a dragon may be tamed, yet it has inverted scales beneath its throat—touch them and it will kill you.

sentences.zh: 人主亦有逆鱗，卿等遂不避犯觸，各進封事。

translations.literal: A sovereign also has inverted scales, yet you did not avoid offending them and each submitted a sealed memorial.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler has his inverted scales too, yet none of you shrank from touching them—you each submitted your sealed memorials.

sentences.zh: 常能如此，朕豈慮有危亡哉！

translations.literal: If you can always be like this, how could I worry about peril and ruin!
translations.idiomatic: If you always act thus, why should I fear ruin!

sentences.zh: 我思卿等此意，豈能暫忘？

translations.literal: When I think of this intention of yours, how could I forget it even for a moment?
translations.idiomatic: When I recall what you have done, how could I ever forget it?

sentences.zh: 故聊設宴樂也。」

translations.literal: Therefore I have casually set out this banquet and music."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I have arranged this feast."

sentences.zh: 仍並賜帛有差。

translations.literal: He also bestowed silk upon them all in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He also rewarded each of them with gifts of silk in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍，行太子右庶子，兼崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally granted Regular Attendant, acting Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent, and concurrently made a scholar of the Chongxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Regular Attendant, acting Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent, and concurrently appointed a scholar of the Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂曰：「國之儲副，自古所重，必擇善人爲之輔佐。

translations.literal: Taizong said to him, "The heir of the state has been valued since antiquity; one must choose good men to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told him, "The heir to the throne has always been a matter of the highest importance, and only worthy men should be chosen to guide him.

sentences.zh: 今太子年在幼沖，志意未定，朕若朝夕見之，可得隨事誡約。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince is still in tender youth and his will is not yet fixed. If I could see him morning and evening, I could admonish and restrain him according to each matter.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is still young and his character is not yet formed. If I could see him every day, I could guide and correct him as occasions arose.

sentences.zh: 今既委以監國，不在目前，知卿志懷貞愨，能敦直道，故輒輟卿於朕，以匡太子，宜知委任輕重也。」

translations.literal: Now that he has been entrusted to oversee the state and is no longer before my eyes, knowing that your will is upright and sincere and that you can earnestly uphold the straight path, I therefore temporarily set you aside from my side to assist the crown prince. You should understand the weight of this commission."
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has been entrusted with regency and is no longer at my side, I know your heart is upright and that you will hold to the straight path. I am therefore releasing you from my immediate service to guide the crown prince—you must understand how weighty this charge is."

sentences.zh: 十年，復授中書侍郎，賜爵南陽縣侯，仍兼太子左庶子。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was again appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, granted the title Marquis of Nanyang County, and still concurrently served as Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was again appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, ennobled as Marquis of Nanyang County, and continued to serve concurrently as Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 正倫出入兩宮，參典機密，甚以干理稱。

translations.literal: Zhenglun moved in and out of the two palaces, participated in confidential affairs, and was greatly praised for practical competence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun moved between the two palaces, took part in confidential state business, and was highly regarded for his administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 時太子承乾有足疾，不能朝謁，好暱近群小。

translations.literal: At the time Crown Prince Chengqian had an ailment of the foot and could not attend court audiences; he liked to draw close to petty men.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Crown Prince Chengqian suffered from a foot ailment that kept him from attending court, and he favored the company of unworthy associates.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂正倫曰：「我兒疾病，乃可事也。

translations.literal: Taizong said to Zhenglun, "My son's illness is a tolerable matter.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told Zhenglun, "My son's illness is not the real problem.

sentences.zh: 但全無令譽，不聞愛賢好善，私所引接，多是小人，卿可察之。

translations.literal: But he entirely lacks a fine reputation; I hear nothing of his loving the worthy and favoring the good. Those he privately draws near are mostly petty men. You should investigate this.
translations.idiomatic: What troubles me is that he has no reputation for virtue, shows no love of worthy men, and keeps company mostly with scoundrels. You must keep a close watch.

sentences.zh: 若教示不得，須來告我。」

translations.literal: If instruction and guidance do not succeed, you must come and tell me."
translations.idiomatic: If your counsel fails to take hold, you must report back to me."

sentences.zh: 正倫數諫不納，乃以太宗語告之，承乾抗表聞奏。

translations.literal: Zhenglun remonstrated several times but was not heeded; he then told Chengqian what Taizong had said, and Chengqian submitted a direct memorial reporting this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun remonstrated repeatedly without effect, then told Chengqian what Taizong had said; Chengqian responded by submitting a memorial directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂正倫曰：「何故漏洩我語？」

translations.literal: Taizong said to Zhenglun, "Why did you leak my words?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong asked Zhenglun, "Why did you reveal what I told you?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「開導不入，故以陛下語嚇之，冀其有懼，或當反善。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Guidance would not enter, so I used Your Majesty's words to frighten him, hoping he would feel fear and perhaps turn back to goodness."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Because my counsel made no impression, I used Your Majesty's words to frighten him, hoping fear might move him to reform."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，出爲谷州刺史，又左授交州都督。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sent him out as Prefect of Gu Prefecture, then demoted him to Area Commander of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and posted him out as prefect of Gu Prefecture, then further demoted him to area commander of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 後承乾構逆，事與侯君集相連，稱遣君集將金帶遺正倫，由是配流驩州。

translations.literal: Later, when Chengqian plotted rebellion, the affair was connected with Hou Junji; it was claimed that Chengqian had sent Junji to present a gold belt to Zhenglun, and because of this Zhenglun was sentenced to exile in Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Chengqian's plot of rebellion came to light and was linked to Hou Junji, it was alleged that Chengqian had sent Junji to present Zhenglun with a gold belt; on this charge Zhenglun was exiled to Huan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，累授黃門侍郎，兼崇賢館學士，尋同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, he was successively appointed Vice Director of the Gate Department, concurrently made a scholar of the Chongxian Hall, and soon made Third Rank Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianqing he was appointed Vice Director of the Gate Department and concurrently made a scholar of the Chongxian Hall; before long he was made Third Rank Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼度支尚書，仍依舊知政事。

translations.literal: In the second year he concurrently served as Minister of the Department of Revenue and still continued as before in managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was additionally appointed Minister of the Department of Revenue while continuing to participate in governance as before.

sentences.zh: 俄拜中書令，兼太子賓客、弘文館學士，進封襄陽縣公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Director of the Secretariat, concurrently made Guest of the Heir Apparent and a scholar of the Hongwen Hall, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Xiangyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Director of the Secretariat, concurrently made Guest of the Heir Apparent and a scholar of the Hongwen Hall, and ennobled as Duke of Xiangyang County.

sentences.zh: 三年，坐與中書令李義府不協，出爲橫州刺史，仍削其封邑。

translations.literal: In the third year, for failing to get along with Director of the Secretariat Li Yifu, he was sent out as Prefect of Heng Prefecture, and his enfeoffment was still reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after falling out with Director of the Secretariat Li Yifu, he was posted out as prefect of Heng Prefecture and stripped of his fief.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 有集十捲行於代。

translations.literal: He had a collected works of ten scrolls circulating in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works, ten scrolls in all, circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：王珪履正不回，忠讜無比，君臣時命，胥會於茲。

translations.literal: The historian remarks: Wang Gui walked the upright path without turning aside; his loyal forthrightness was without parallel. The fates of ruler and minister all converged at this moment.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Wang Gui held unwaveringly to the upright path, and his loyal candor was without equal—the fates of ruler and minister alike met at this juncture.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「自天祐之，吉無不利。」

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says, "When Heaven assists him, auspiciousness—nothing is unfavorable."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "When Heaven lends its aid, good fortune follows—nothing goes amiss."

sentences.zh: 叔玠有焉。

translations.literal: Shujie had this.
translations.idiomatic: Of this Wang Shujie was a true exemplar.

sentences.zh: 戴胄兩朝仕官，一乃心力，刑無僭濫，事有箴規。

translations.literal: Dai Zhou served as an official through two reigns with unified heart and strength; in punishments there was no excess or abuse, and in affairs there was admonition and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhou served through two reigns with undivided devotion; under his hand the law was never abused, and his counsel was always to the point.

sentences.zh: 雖學術不能求備，而匡益自可濟時，亦所謂巧於任大矣。

translations.literal: Although his learning could not be sought to completeness, his corrective benefit by itself could aid the age—this too is what is called being skillful at undertaking great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Though his learning was not encyclopedic, the good he did was enough to serve the times—this is what it means to be adept at bearing great responsibility.

sentences.zh: 文本文傾江海，忠貫雪霜，申慈父之冤，匡明主之業，及委繁劇，俄致暴終。

translations.literal: Wenben's writing poured like rivers and seas; his loyalty pierced through frost and snow. He pleaded the grievance of a loving father, rectified the enterprise of an enlightened ruler, and when entrusted with heavy and urgent duties, soon met a sudden end.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben's prose flowed like rivers and seas, and his loyalty was steadfast as frost and snow. He vindicated a father's wronged honor, strengthened an enlightened ruler's enterprise, and when burdened with crushing duties met a sudden, violent end.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「小心翼翼，昭事上帝。」

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says, "With cautious care and trembling awe, clearly serving the Lord on High."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "Be reverent and cautious in serving the Lord on High."

sentences.zh: 所謂憂能傷人，不復永年矣。

translations.literal: This is what is called worry being able to harm a man—he did not again enjoy long years.
translations.idiomatic: So it is said that worry can destroy a man—he did not live out his full span of years.

sentences.zh: 洎羲而下，登清要者數十人。

translations.literal: Down from Xi, several dozen reached important and prestigious posts.
translations.idiomatic: From Xi downward, several dozen kinsmen rose to prestigious offices.

sentences.zh: 積善之道，焉可忽諸？

translations.literal: The way of accumulating goodness—how can it be neglected?
translations.idiomatic: The way of accumulated virtue—how can it be lightly dismissed?

sentences.zh: 正倫以能文被舉，以直道見委，參典機密，出入兩宮，斯謂得時。

translations.literal: Zhenglun was recommended for his literary ability, entrusted for his upright path, participated in confidential affairs, and moved in and out of the two palaces—this is called catching the right moment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun was promoted for his literary gifts, entrusted for his integrity, and moved between the two palaces handling state secrets—truly he had found his moment.

sentences.zh: 然被承乾金帶之譏，孰與夫薏苡之謗，士大夫慎之。

translations.literal: Yet he suffered the reproach of Chengqian's gold belt—how does that compare with the slander of foxtail millet? Gentlemen should be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he fell under suspicion for accepting Chengqian's gold belt—a stain no less damaging than the foxtail-millet calumny that destroyed Ma Yuan. Let men of honor take heed.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：五靈嘉瑞，出系汙隆。

translations.literal: In praise: The five auspicious numina and blessed omens emerge according to the rise and fall of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: The five auspicious signs and blessed portents appear according to whether the times are in decline or ascent.

sentences.zh: 人中麟鳳，王、戴諸公。

translations.literal: Among men, qilin and phoenix—Lords Wang, Dai, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Among men, qilin and phoenix—the likes of Wang, Dai, and their fellows.

sentences.zh: 動必由禮，言皆匡躬。

translations.literal: In action they always followed ritual; in speech they all set the ruler straight.
translations.idiomatic: In action they always followed ritual; in speech they all set the ruler on the right path.

sentences.zh: 獻規納諫，貞觀之風。

translations.literal: Offering counsel and accepting remonstrance — such was the spirit of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: Offering counsel and accepting remonstrance — such was the spirit of the Zhenguan era.
